parts.label: Pressure transducers
parts.what: Two 0–250 bar sensors on the pressure and work galleries, read by the Opta’s analogue inputs: the controller sees how hard the machine is working and when it is stalled against relief.

parts.label: Return line
parts.what: From the manifold’s tank gallery back over the cube to its return coupler: inside the cube the oil runs through its six-tube cooler and its return filter into its reservoir, the oil’s way home after doing its work.
specs: Manifold T → the cube’s return coupler → cooler → filter → reservoir

parts.label: Lift cylinder hoses, left
parts.what: The two lines from the arms’ valve to the lift cylinder: oil into the cap end raises the arm, into the rod end lowers it. Both lift cylinders are fed in parallel.

parts.label: Lift cylinder hoses, right
parts.what: The two lines from the arms’ valve to the lift cylinder: oil into the cap end raises the arm, into the rod end lowers it. Both lift cylinders are fed in parallel.

parts.label: Bucket cylinder hoses
parts.what: From the bucket valve over to the arm pivots and along the arms to the bucket cylinders on the cross beam. Where they cross the pivot they hang in loose loops, so the arms can rise without stretching them.

parts.label: Arm side plates, left (P9, P10)
parts.what: Two L-shaped 1/4" plates either side of the arm’s tube, cut on the CNC plasma table: they make the arm’s bend, carry the pivot plates at its back, the lift bracket under it and the bucket’s pin at its tip.
parts.moves: Swing up and down with the arm about the pivot pin.

parts.label: Arm main tube, left (T4)
parts.what: The arm’s backbone: a 6×2 rectangular tube from the pivot to the bend, and on down the drop leg towards the bucket, sandwiched between the side plates and bolted through them.
parts.moves: Swings with the arm.

parts.label: Arm pivot, left (R2, T6, P11, F1)
parts.what: The joint the whole loader turns on: a 1½" 4140 pin through both plates of the sandwich and a DOM tube in the arm, the tube welded into two round 6" plates that bolt to the arm with five 1/2" bolts, a big 1½-6 nut on each end of the pin.
parts.moves: The DOM tube turns on the pin as the arm swings; the pin stays.

parts.label: Lift cylinder bracket, left
parts.what: Two gusset plates under the arm, 828 mm out from the pivot, with a 1" bolt for the lift cylinder’s rod eye: where the cylinder pushes the arm up.
parts.moves: Swings with the arm.
specs: 828.5 mm along the arm, 114.3 mm under it

parts.label: Arm side plates, right (P9, P10)
parts.what: Two L-shaped 1/4" plates either side of the arm’s tube, cut on the CNC plasma table: they make the arm’s bend, carry the pivot plates at its back, the lift bracket under it and the bucket’s pin at its tip.
parts.moves: Swing up and down with the arm about the pivot pin.

parts.label: Arm main tube, right (T4)
parts.what: The arm’s backbone: a 6×2 rectangular tube from the pivot to the bend, and on down the drop leg towards the bucket, sandwiched between the side plates and bolted through them.
parts.moves: Swings with the arm.

parts.label: Arm pivot, right (R2, T6, P11, F1)
parts.what: The joint the whole loader turns on: a 1½" 4140 pin through both plates of the sandwich and a DOM tube in the arm, the tube welded into two round 6" plates that bolt to the arm with five 1/2" bolts, a big 1½-6 nut on each end of the pin.
parts.moves: The DOM tube turns on the pin as the arm swings; the pin stays.

parts.label: Lift cylinder bracket, right
parts.what: Two gusset plates under the arm, 828 mm out from the pivot, with a 1" bolt for the lift cylinder’s rod eye: where the cylinder pushes the arm up.
parts.moves: Swings with the arm.
specs: 828.5 mm along the arm, 114.3 mm under it

parts.label: Arm cross beam (T3, A5)
parts.what: The 6×2 tube tying the two arms together a little forward of the pivot, so they rise as one, bolted to each arm through two angles. The bucket cylinders hang from its underside.
parts.moves: Swings with the arms.
parts.drive: The lift cylinders, through the arms

parts.label: Bucket cylinder lugs (U1, R3)
parts.what: Two short pieces of 3×3 tube welded under the cross beam, each with a 3/4" clevis pin for a bucket cylinder’s base eye.
parts.moves: Swing with the arms.

parts.label: Lift cylinder barrel, left
parts.what: The lift cylinder’s barrel, pinned to the frame low behind the arm pivot inside the sandwich’s gap. Oil pumped into its cap end pushes the piston and rod out, raising the arm; into the rod end, it pulls them back.
parts.moves: Tilts about its base pin as the arm rises, so it always points at the bracket.
parts.drive: Oil from the arms’ valve (D5 up, D6 down)
specs: 3,674 kg arms down, 1,258 kg at full height

parts.label: Lift cylinder rod, left
parts.what: The chromed 1½" rod and the piston on its inner end: it slides out of the barrel under pressure, its eye pinned to the arm’s bracket.
parts.moves: Slides out of and back into the barrel, turning with the arm about the bracket bolt.
parts.drive: The oil pressure on its piston

parts.label: Bucket cylinder barrel, left
parts.what: The bucket cylinder’s barrel, hung by its base eye from a lug under the cross beam: it rides with the arms and pushes on the bucket’s top.
parts.moves: Rises with the arms and tilts about its lug pin as the bucket turns.
parts.drive: Oil from the bucket valve (D7 curl, D8 dump)
specs: up to 35.2 kN dump, 26.4 kN curl

parts.label: Bucket cylinder rod, left
parts.what: Its chromed rod, pinned to the lug on the bucket’s back: pushed out it tips the bucket forward to dump, drawn in it curls the bucket back to hold its load.
parts.moves: Slides out and in, turning with the bucket.
parts.drive: The oil pressure on its piston

parts.label: Lift cylinder barrel, right
parts.what: The lift cylinder’s barrel, pinned to the frame low behind the arm pivot inside the sandwich’s gap. Oil pumped into its cap end pushes the piston and rod out, raising the arm; into the rod end, it pulls them back.
parts.moves: Tilts about its base pin as the arm rises, so it always points at the bracket.
parts.drive: Oil from the arms’ valve (D5 up, D6 down)
specs: 3,674 kg arms down, 1,258 kg at full height

parts.label: Lift cylinder rod, right
parts.what: The chromed 1½" rod and the piston on its inner end: it slides out of the barrel under pressure, its eye pinned to the arm’s bracket.
parts.moves: Slides out of and back into the barrel, turning with the arm about the bracket bolt.
parts.drive: The oil pressure on its piston

parts.label: Bucket cylinder barrel, right
parts.what: The bucket cylinder’s barrel, hung by its base eye from a lug under the cross beam: it rides with the arms and pushes on the bucket’s top.
parts.moves: Rises with the arms and tilts about its lug pin as the bucket turns.
parts.drive: Oil from the bucket valve (D7 curl, D8 dump)
specs: up to 35.2 kN dump, 26.4 kN curl

parts.label: Bucket cylinder rod, right
parts.what: Its chromed rod, pinned to the lug on the bucket’s back: pushed out it tips the bucket forward to dump, drawn in it curls the bucket back to hold its load.
parts.moves: Slides out and in, turning with the bucket.
parts.drive: The oil pressure on its piston

parts.label: Bucket shell (P12, P13, P14)
parts.what: The bucket: a back plate, a bottom and two sides of 1/4" plate welded into an open box 1,100 mm wide, 600 deep and 450 high, about a third of a cubic metre heaped.
parts.moves: Turns about the pins at the arms’ tips: curled back to carry, tipped forward to dump; and rises with the arms.

parts.label: Cutting edge (P19)
parts.what: A 3/4" bar along the bucket’s front lip, the part that bites into the ground and wears: bolted or welded on so it can be replaced.
parts.moves: With the bucket.

parts.label: Bucket pivot lugs and pins (U2, R4)
parts.what: Two 3×3 tube lugs on the bucket’s back, pinned through the arms’ tips with 1" pins: the hinge the bucket turns on. OSE’s own analysis flags this joint as overloaded at relief; a quick-attach plate (46 × 18") is planned here instead.
parts.moves: The lugs turn on the pins with the bucket.
specs: Skid-steer quick attach, 1,168 × 457 mm, 1" lock pins

parts.label: Bucket cylinder lugs (U3)
parts.what: Two lugs high on the bucket’s back for the bucket cylinders’ rod eyes: the higher above the pivot, the more leverage the cylinders have to break the bucket out of the ground.
parts.moves: With the bucket.

parts.label: Platform deck (P15)
parts.what: A 1/4" plate to stand on behind the machine, punched with a grid of anti-slip holes. The machine has no seat and no cab: it is meant to be driven by radio, the deck is for riding when that is easier.
parts.moves: Folds up about its pivot pins to stow, down to stand on.
parts.drive: By hand; locked by two 5/8" pins

parts.label: Platform angles (A7, A8)
parts.what: The 2×2 angles under the deck: two short side arms that reach forward to its pivot pins, two long transverse angles across its front and back edges.
parts.moves: Fold with the deck.

parts.label: Platform pivot brackets, pins and lock pins (P16, R5, F2)
parts.what: Two brackets bolted inside the inner panels carry the deck’s 1" pivot pins; a 5/8" hitch pin through each bracket, 60 mm from the pivot, locks the deck down or up.
parts.moves: The brackets stay; the deck turns on their pins.

parts.label: Tractor node enclosure
parts.what: An IP65 box with a clear lid holding the machine’s brain, mounted on the Power Cube’s top in front of the valves. Its harness leaves through Deutsch DT connectors.

parts.label: Portenta X8 on its Max Carrier
parts.what: The tractor’s main computer: an Arduino Portenta X8 (a Linux i.MX8M Mini with an STM32H747 beside it) plugged into a Portenta Max Carrier with its LoRa radio. It receives the handheld’s commands at 20 Hz, decides which source wins (handheld, base station, autonomy), and drives the Opta over Modbus.
parts.moves: Nothing moves; it ticks a 10 Hz watchdog, or every coil drops.
specs: An H7-only option is proposed (export rules on the X8)

parts.label: Opta WiFi with D1608S and A0602
parts.what: The machine’s hands: an Arduino Opta PLC on a DIN rail with two expansions. The D1608S’s eight solid-state outputs switch the eight valve coils; the A0602 puts out 0–10 V to the flow valve’s driver and reads the battery, both pressures and the oil temperature. The Opta’s own relays kill the engine, sound the horn and beacon, release the park brake.
specs: Modbus slave; relays R1 kill, R2 beacon/horn, R3 brake, R4 spare
8 × SSR to the coils, flyback diodes; inputs ignition, E-stop, mode
AO1/AO2 0–10 V to the EFC; AI battery, 2 pressures, coolant, oil temp

parts.label: EFC driver (Burkert 8605)
parts.what: A small DIN-rail amplifier turning the Opta’s 0–10 V into the coil current the proportional flow valve needs.

parts.label: Safety relay and E-stop loop
parts.what: A Phoenix PSR dual-channel safety relay: while the E-stop loop is closed it holds the 12 V valve rail and the engine’s run circuit on. Press any E-stop (on the machine or the handheld) and it drops both, whatever the computers think.
specs: 12 V valve rail and engine kill (30 A relay)
Latching mushrooms on tractor and handheld

parts.label: Fuses and power path
parts.what: From the battery: a 175 A master cut-off, an EMI filter, a 20 A main fuse, then eight 5 A fuses, one per valve coil; a small 18650 cell keeps the computer alive through cranking.

parts.label: Status lamps and buzzer
parts.what: Three lamps on the lid — POWER, LINK, FAULT — and a buzzer: at a glance, is it powered, is it hearing the handheld, has it stopped itself.

parts.label: GPS and IMU boards
parts.what: A u-blox NEO-M9N GPS (an RTK ZED-F9P later, for centimetres) and a BNO086 motion sensor: where the machine is, which way it faces, how it tilts — for the base station’s map, and for warning before it tips.

parts.label: Valve and sensor harness
parts.what: The wiring from the node box to the eight valve coils (DIN plugs), the flow valve, the pressure sensors, the engine’s kill and ignition sense, and up the mast.
specs: Deutsch DT at the box, DIN 43650-A at the coils

parts.label: Master cut-off switch
parts.what: A red key on the Power Cube battery’s positive lead, its key through the back wall: turned off, nothing on the machine is live — for servicing and for leaving it.
parts.moves: Turned by hand.

parts.label: Antenna mast
parts.what: A steel pole on the back wall lifting the radio, GPS and cameras clear of the steel around them.

parts.label: LoRa antenna
parts.what: The whip for the control radio: raw LoRa with OSE’s own frame format, every command 16 bytes, encrypted, twenty times a second. Lose it for a second and the machine stops itself.

parts.label: GPS antenna
parts.what: A patch antenna on the mast’s top plate, seeing the sky for the GPS receiver.

parts.label: Cameras
parts.what: USB cameras looking forward over the bucket and back over the deck, streamed to the base station so the machine can be driven out of sight. Up to four can be fitted.
specs: Arducam IMX335 on a Raspberry Pi 4

parts.label: Warning beacon and horn
parts.what: An amber beacon on the back wall that flashes whenever the machine moves, and a horn beside it, both on the Opta’s relay R2: a machine with nobody on it has to say it is coming.
parts.moves: Flashes while the machine moves.

parts.label: Beacon lamp
parts.what: The beacon’s lamp: lit, it is flashing.
parts.moves: Flashes while the machine moves.

parts.label: E-stop on the machine
parts.what: A latching red mushroom on the back wall: pushed, it opens the safety relay’s loop, dropping the valves (everything holds where it is) and killing the engine. Twisted out, the machine can be started again.
parts.moves: Pushed in to stop; twisted to release.

parts.label: Handheld remote
parts.what: How the LifeTrac is driven: a small IP54 box on an Arduino MKR WAN 1310 with two joysticks, an E-stop, four buttons and a screen, its own LoRa radio. Here it sits in its holster on the back wall.
specs: Base station web UI; research build: BLE (DroidPad), Wi-Fi/MQTT, ROS2

parts.label: Handheld joystick, left
parts.what: The left stick: drive: forward and back on Y, steer on X (tank steering). A 10 % dead zone in the middle; the stick’s deflection sets the flow valve’s opening, so a little deflection is a slow, fine movement.
parts.moves: Tilts as the machine is driven (watch it in the moves).
specs: drive: forward and back on Y, steer on X (tank steering)
SparkFun Qwiic joysticks on an ESP32

parts.label: Handheld joystick, right
parts.what: The right stick: loader: arms up and down on Y, bucket curl and dump on X. A 10 % dead zone in the middle; the stick’s deflection sets the flow valve’s opening, so a little deflection is a slow, fine movement.
parts.moves: Tilts as the machine is driven (watch it in the moves).
specs: loader: arms up and down on Y, bucket curl and dump on X
SparkFun Qwiic joysticks on an ESP32

steps: Bolt the frame: floor plate and its angle runs, back and front walls, motor plates, inner and outer side panels, cross tubes
Mount the four wheel units: motors on the motor plates, shafts through the bearings, hubs, wheels
Lift in the Power Cube, already built on its own, and pin it to its cradle: engine, pump, tanks, cooler and battery come in one piece
Plumb the hydraulics: the flow valve and the valve manifold on the cube, the pressure and return lines to its couplers, hoses out to the motors
Hang the loader arms on their pivot pins and bolt in the cross beam
Pin in the lift and bucket cylinders
Pin on the bucket
Bolt on the folding platform
Wire the controller: node box, boards, safety relay, master switch, mast, antennas, cameras, beacon, E-stop; pair the handheld

de87e0f6ab67b33ef730738833d6825c8a27800b.label: Pickup: Pickup
de87e0f6ab67b33ef730738833d6825c8a27800b.note: 5.35 × 1.86 m, 1.82 m to its roof; a double cab, four doors and five seats; a 1.78 m bed with a tailgate; 1,750 kg, 950 kg payload

assemblies.label: Chassis and suspension
assemblies.note: The ladder frame, kicked up over the rear axle; double wishbones and coil-overs in front with the rack-and-pinion, a live axle on leaf springs behind.

assemblies.label: Wheels and brakes
assemblies.note: Four 265/70 R16 tyres on steel wheels and a fifth under the bed; vented discs and callipers in front, drums behind.

assemblies.label: Engine
assemblies.note: A 2.5 L four-cylinder turbo-diesel under the bonnet, 75 kW and 240 N·m.

assemblies.label: Gearbox and drive
assemblies.note: The clutch, the 5-speed gearbox, the two-piece propshaft and the rear axle’s crown wheel and pinion.

assemblies.label: Cooling, fuel and power
assemblies.note: The radiator in the nose, the battery and the air filter beside the engine, the fuel tank under the cab, the exhaust.

assemblies.label: Cab
assemblies.note: The steel cab on its rubber mounts: its sides, nose, bonnet, roof and back wall, the floor, the glass, the lights and bumpers.

assemblies.label: Doors
assemblies.note: Four doors, each on two hinges at its front edge.

assemblies.label: Seats and dashboard
assemblies.note: The dashboard and its gauges, the steering wheel and pedals, the console and the lever, two seats in front and a bench for three behind.

assemblies.label: Bed and tailgate
assemblies.note: The steel bed behind the cab on its own mounts: its floor, its double-walled sides and wheel tubs, the tailgate on its hinges and check cables.

parts.label: Ladder frame
parts.what: Two boxed steel rails the length of the pickup, low under the cab and kicked up over the rear axle so it can rise under the bed, joined by crossmembers; the cab and the bed sit on it on rubber mounts, the engine between its rails. A dropped crossmember carries the front suspension, another the gearbox’s tail, and the hitch’s receiver is welded to the last.

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, front left
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road and steers with the knuckle (shown turning 10 times slower).
parts.drive: The road; steered by the knuckle

parts.label: Brake disc, front left
parts.what: A vented cast-iron disc bolted to the hub between it and the wheel: the calliper squeezes it, and its vanes pump air through it to carry the heat away.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; the calliper stops it

parts.label: Brake calliper, front left
parts.what: A floating calliper over the disc’s back edge: the brake fluid pushes its piston, which presses the inner pad on the disc and pulls the outer pad on from the other side.

parts.label: Steering knuckle, front left
parts.what: The cast upright between the two wishbones’ ball joints: it carries the hub’s bearings on its spindle, the calliper on its bracket, and turns about the line through its ball joints (the kingpin axis) when the tie rod pulls its steering arm.
parts.moves: Steers about its ball joints; rides up and down with the wheel.
parts.drive: The tie rod, from the steering

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, front right
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road and steers with the knuckle (shown turning 10 times slower).
parts.drive: The road; its brake stops it

parts.label: Brake disc, front right
parts.what: A vented cast-iron disc bolted to the hub between it and the wheel: the calliper squeezes it, and its vanes pump air through it to carry the heat away.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; the calliper stops it

parts.label: Brake calliper, front right
parts.what: A floating calliper over the disc’s back edge: the brake fluid pushes its piston, which presses the inner pad on the disc and pulls the outer pad on from the other side.

parts.label: Steering knuckle, front right
parts.what: The cast upright between the two wishbones’ ball joints: it carries the hub’s bearings on its spindle, the calliper on its bracket, and turns about the line through its ball joints (the kingpin axis) when the tie rod pulls its steering arm.
parts.moves: Steers about its ball joints; rides up and down with the wheel.
parts.drive: The tie rod, from the steering

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, rear left
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).

parts.label: Brake drum, rear left
parts.what: A finned cast-iron drum on the hub: two shoes inside it, pushed out by the wheel cylinder, rub on its inner face. Cheap, sealed from the dust and good for a handbrake.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; its shoes stop it

parts.label: Backing plate, rear left
parts.what: The pressed-steel plate that closes the drum: it carries the two shoes, their springs, the wheel cylinder and the handbrake’s lever, bolted to the axle’s end.

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, rear right
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).

parts.label: Brake drum, rear right
parts.what: A finned cast-iron drum on the hub: two shoes inside it, pushed out by the wheel cylinder, rub on its inner face. Cheap, sealed from the dust and good for a handbrake.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; its shoes stop it

parts.label: Backing plate, rear right
parts.what: The pressed-steel plate that closes the drum: it carries the two shoes, their springs, the wheel cylinder and the handbrake’s lever, bolted to the axle’s end.

parts.label: Spare wheel
parts.what: A fifth wheel and tyre hung flat under the back of the bed on a cable: a crank through the bumper winds it down.

parts.label: Upper wishbone, front left
parts.what: A pressed and welded A-arm from two rubber bushes on the frame to the knuckle’s upper ball joint: with the lower arm it holds the wheel upright as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks on its springs.

parts.label: Lower wishbone, front left
parts.what: The longer, stronger lower A-arm: it carries the coil spring’s load from the knuckle’s lower ball joint to the frame and takes the braking forces.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks.

parts.label: Coil spring and damper, front left
parts.what: A coil spring round a telescopic damper from the lower arm up to its tower on the frame: the spring carries the body, the damper’s oil forced through its valves stops it bouncing.
parts.moves: Shortens as the load or the climb presses the front down; lengthens as it lifts.
parts.drive: The road, through the lower arm

parts.label: Tie rod, front left
parts.what: From the steering rack’s end to the knuckle’s steering arm: as the rack slides, it pushes or pulls the arm and turns the wheel about its ball joints. Its threaded end sets the toe.
parts.moves: Follows the rack and the wheel.

parts.label: Upper wishbone, front right
parts.what: A pressed and welded A-arm from two rubber bushes on the frame to the knuckle’s upper ball joint: with the lower arm it holds the wheel upright as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks on its springs.

parts.label: Lower wishbone, front right
parts.what: The longer, stronger lower A-arm: it carries the coil spring’s load from the knuckle’s lower ball joint to the frame and takes the braking forces.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks.

parts.label: Coil spring and damper, front right
parts.what: A coil spring round a telescopic damper from the lower arm up to its tower on the frame: the spring carries the body, the damper’s oil forced through its valves stops it bouncing.
parts.moves: Shortens as the load or the climb presses the front down; lengthens as it lifts.
parts.drive: The road, through the lower arm

parts.label: Tie rod, front right
parts.what: From the steering rack’s end to the knuckle’s steering arm: as the rack slides, it pushes or pulls the arm and turns the wheel about its ball joints. Its threaded end sets the toe.
parts.moves: Follows the rack and the wheel.

parts.label: Steering rack
parts.what: A rack-and-pinion box across the front: the steering wheel’s shaft turns the pinion, the pinion slides the toothed rack sideways, the rack pushes and pulls the tie rods.
parts.moves: The rack slides as the wheel is turned (held straight here).
parts.drive: The steering wheel, through its shaft and universal joints

parts.label: Rear axle housing
parts.what: The banjo housing: a pressed-steel bowl round the differential with a tube out to each wheel, its spring seats welded on. It carries the vehicle’s rear and its load straight to the wheels.

parts.label: Crown wheel, pinion and half-shafts
parts.what: The propshaft turns the pinion, the pinion turns the crown wheel 4.1 times slower and a right angle round; the differential’s gears on the crown wheel share its torque between the half-shafts, letting the outer wheel turn faster in a bend.
parts.moves: The pinion turns with the propshaft, the crown wheel and half-shafts with the wheels (shown slowed).

parts.label: Leaf springs and U-bolts
parts.what: Two packs of 5 steel leaves, each clamped to the axle by two U-bolts, its front eye on a hanger, its back eye on a swinging shackle: they carry the load and locate the axle. They flatten as the load grows.
parts.moves: Flatten as the body sinks onto the axle, arch again as it lifts.

parts.label: Spring hangers and shackles
parts.what: Under the frame: a fixed hanger for each spring’s front eye and a swinging shackle for its back eye, so the leaves can lengthen as they flatten.

parts.label: Rear dampers
parts.what: Telescopic dampers from the axle up to the frame, leaning in: oil forced through their valves turns the body’s bounce into heat.
parts.moves: Shorten as the body sinks, lengthen as it lifts.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cylinder block, 2.5 L turbo-diesel
parts.what: The cast-iron block: four 93 mm bores bored through its deck, water round them, the crankcase under them with five bulkheads that carry the crankshaft’s main bearings. Everything else on the engine bolts to it.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cylinder head
parts.what: The aluminium head closing the bores: its ports, the valves’ seats and guides, the camshaft’s bearings and the injectors’ wells; held down on its gasket by ten long bolts.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cam cover
parts.what: The pressed cover over the camshaft and valves, keeping their oil in; its cap is where the oil goes in.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Camshaft and valves
parts.what: One overhead camshaft, turned by the timing belt at half the crank’s speed: its lobes push the eight valves open through their buckets, their springs close them.
parts.moves: Turns at half the crank’s speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.what: The forged crankshaft on its five main bearings: its four pins, two up and two down, turn the pistons’ push into torque; the counterweights opposite them balance it.
parts.moves: Turns at the engine’s speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Pistons
parts.what: Four cast-aluminium pistons, the combustion bowl in each crown where the fuel is sprayed, three rings sealing them in their bores; each pushed down by its burning charge.
parts.moves: Up and down their bores (shown 40 times slower).
parts.drive: The burning charge; they drive the rods

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Connecting rods
parts.what: Forged steel I-section rods from each piston’s pin to its crank pin, their big ends split and bolted round the pins on shell bearings.
parts.moves: Swing and slide with the pistons.
parts.drive: The pistons; they drive the crankshaft

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Flywheel
parts.what: A heavy steel disc on the crank’s back end: it carries the engine through the strokes between firings and is the clutch’s friction face; the starter turns its ring gear.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Clutch
parts.what: A friction disc pressed against the flywheel by the cover’s diaphragm spring: it passes the engine’s torque to the gearbox, and slips to let the vehicle pull away.
parts.moves: Turns with the flywheel; slips while it pulls away.
parts.drive: The pedal, through its cable and release bearing

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Sump
parts.what: The pressed-steel oil pan under the crankcase, deep at one end where the pump’s pickup draws the oil; its drain plug at the bottom.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Timing belt and cover
parts.what: A toothed belt from the crank to the camshaft and the injection pump, both turning at half the crank’s speed so each valve and each squirt of fuel comes at its stroke; under its plastic cover.
parts.moves: The belt runs round its three sprockets.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Accessory belt and water pump
parts.what: A V-belt from the crank’s pulley (its damper behind) round the water pump’s and the alternator’s: the pump drives the coolant through the block, the head and the radiator.
parts.moves: The belt and pulleys turn with the engine.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Alternator
parts.what: Turned by the belt at about 2.5 times the crank’s speed, it charges the battery and runs the lights.
parts.moves: Its rotor and pulley turn with the belt.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Fan and viscous coupling
parts.what: Seven plastic blades on the water pump’s hub through a viscous coupling: it pulls air through the radiator, slipping when the air is cool.
parts.moves: Turns with the water pump.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Injection pump, lines and injectors
parts.what: The distributor pump, turned by the timing belt, meters the fuel and squeezes it to some 300 bar into each injector in turn through its own steel line, at the moment its piston comes up on compression; the glow plugs on the other side warm the chambers for a cold start.
parts.moves: Its shaft turns at half the crank’s speed.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Intake manifold
parts.what: The cast-aluminium manifold that shares the air from the filter among the four inlet ports.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Exhaust manifold and turbocharger
parts.what: The cast-iron manifold gathers the four cylinders’ gas into the turbocharger’s turbine; its compressor on the same shaft pushes the air into the intake at up to 0.9 bar.
parts.moves: The turbo’s shaft spins at up to 150,000 rpm (not shown turning).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Oil filter and dipstick
parts.what: A spin-on full-flow filter that the oil pump pushes all the oil through before the bearings; the dipstick to check its level.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Starter motor
parts.what: A 12 V motor on the bellhousing’s flange: its solenoid throws its pinion into the flywheel’s ring gear and it spins the engine to start it.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Engine and gearbox mounts
parts.what: Rubber blocks between the engine’s brackets and the frame, and under the gearbox’s tail: they carry its weight and its torque and keep its shake out of the body.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Bellhousing
parts.what: The cast-aluminium bell bolted to the block’s back face round the flywheel and clutch, carrying the gearbox and the starter.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Gearbox, 5 speeds
parts.what: A 5-speed manual gearbox: the input shaft from the clutch drives the layshaft below it, whose gears turn the gears riding free on the output shaft; the lever slides a synchro collar to lock one of them to the shaft (top gear locks the input to the output straight).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Shafts and gears
parts.what: Inside the case: the input shaft and its gear, the layshaft and its cluster, the output shaft with the gears that ride on it, all in constant mesh; the synchro collars between them.
parts.moves: The shafts and gears turn (shown 40 times slower).
specs: Constant, helical in the case [simplified straight here]

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Gear lever
parts.what: The lever and its rod into the gearbox’s selector: across to pick a gate, forward and back to choose a gear.
parts.moves: Moved by hand; the solver changes gear by itself.

parts.label: Propshaft (two pieces)
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: Two thin-walled steel tubes from the gearbox to the axle, joined over a rubber-mounted centre bearing under the floor, a universal joint at each end of each to follow the axle as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Turns at the gearbox’s output speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.label: Centre bearing bracket
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: A pressed-steel bracket under the cab’s floor holding the propshaft’s centre bearing in its rubber.

parts.label: Radiator and shroud
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: In the nose behind the grille: the engine’s coolant runs down through the radiator’s finned tubes and gives its heat to the air the road and the engine’s fan pull through it; the shroud round the fan makes it pull through all of the core.
specs: About a third of the fuel’s heat at full load

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: The starting battery on its tray over the right front wheel: it cranks the engine and heats the glow plugs; the alternator charges it.

parts.label: Air filter and intake
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: The engine breathes through a paper element in this box over the left front wheel, then through a duct to the turbocharger’s compressor.

parts.label: Fuel tank
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: A 76 L pressed-steel tank outside the right rail under the cab’s back, hung on two straps; its filler neck runs up to the cap on the bed’s side.

parts.label: Exhaust and silencer
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: From the turbocharger down and back under the cab through the silencer, over the axle and out under the back on the right, hung on rubber loops.

parts.label: Cab sides and front wings
parts.what: The two pressed-steel sides of the cab and its front wings in one: the four door openings, the pillars between them, the front wheels’ arches cut in; the wheel housings and inner wings inside.

parts.label: Nose, roof and back wall
parts.what: The cab’s ends and top: the nose with the grille’s opening, the cowl under the windscreen, the windscreen’s frame, the roof, and the back wall with its window; every edge rounded onto the sides.

parts.label: Bonnet
parts.what: The steel bonnet over the engine, hinged at its back edge under the windscreen, a stay to hold it up; its rounded edges meet the wings.

parts.label: Windscreen and back window
parts.what: The laminated windscreen raked back over the bonnet, and the toughened window in the cab’s back wall.

parts.label: Floor, firewall and lining
parts.what: The cab’s steel floor on the frame’s mounts, a tunnel down its middle over the gearbox and the propshaft, the firewall between the engine and the cab, a rubber mat over the floor; the headlining under the roof and the trim on the back wall.

parts.label: Bumpers, plates and mounts
parts.what: A steel bumper in front, a step bumper behind with the hitch’s receiver through it, both on brackets to the frame; the number plates (blank); the cab’s rubber mounts on the frame’s outriggers.

parts.label: Headlights and grille
parts.what: Two headlights with their indicators beside them in the nose, the grille between them that lets the air to the radiator, the side repeaters on the wings.

parts.label: Wipers
parts.what: Two wipers parked at the windscreen’s foot, driven by one motor under the cowl.

parts.label: Front door, left (the driver’s)
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles, its mirror on its front corner. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Front door, right
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles, its mirror on its front corner. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Rear door, left
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Rear door, right
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Front seats
parts.what: The driver’s seat and the passenger’s, on runners to slide them, their backs raked, a headrest on each.

parts.label: Rear bench
parts.what: A bench for three across the back of the cab, upright against its back wall.

parts.label: Dashboard and gauges
parts.what: The moulded dashboard under the windscreen: the speedometer and the rev counter in their binnacle before the driver, the radio and the heater’s controls in the middle, four vents, the glovebox before the passenger.
parts.moves: Its needles show the speed and the engine’s revs.
specs: Speed to 180 km/h, revs to 5,000 rpm

parts.label: Steering wheel and column
parts.what: The wheel on its column through the dashboard to the firewall, where a shaft with two universal joints runs down past the engine to the rack.
parts.moves: Turned by the driver (held straight here).

parts.label: Pedals, console and handbrake
parts.what: Clutch, brake and accelerator hanging from under the dashboard; the console over the tunnel between the front seats with the gear lever through it and the handbrake beside it, which pulls the rear drums’ shoes by cable.

parts.label: Bed sides and front wall
parts.what: The bed’s double walls: the painted outer skins with the rear wheels’ arches cut in, the inner walls the load rubs against, the caps along their tops, the front wall behind the cab, the back posts carrying the lights; the wheel housings under the floor and the tubs over them.

parts.label: Bed floor
parts.what: The bed’s floor: a ribbed steel sheet on four bearers across the frame’s rails, coated against wear; eight hooks along its edges to tie the load down. What is put on the bed stands on it.

parts.label: Tail lights
parts.what: The tail, brake, indicator and reversing lights on the bed’s back posts.

parts.label: Tailgate
parts.what: The bed’s back wall on two hinges along its bottom edge: unlatched by its handle it drops back to lie level with the floor, held there by two steel check cables, to load the bed or to carry something longer than it.
parts.moves: Drops 90° on its hinges.

parts.label: Tailgate sill and hinges
parts.what: The sill along the bed’s back edge that the tailgate’s hinge pins turn in.

steps: Weld the frame and hang the suspension, the axle and the steering on it
Bolt on the wheels and brakes
Drop in the engine on its mounts
Bolt on the gearbox; fit the propshaft and the axle’s gears
Fit the radiator, battery, air filter, fuel tank and exhaust
Lower the cab onto the frame; fit the glass, lights and bumpers
Hang the doors
Fit the dashboard, the steering wheel, the seats
Bolt the bed on behind the cab and hang its tailgate

sources.label: Road load and rolling resistance (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)

35387517b3ac7208c296877708c5c155d591eef8.label: Pickup: With a Power Cube
35387517b3ac7208c296877708c5c155d591eef8.note: the Power Cube (v3) carried whole on its bed and strapped down, every part of it its own here too; its 181 kg on the springs and in the solver

assemblies.label: Chassis and suspension
assemblies.note: The ladder frame, kicked up over the rear axle; double wishbones and coil-overs in front with the rack-and-pinion, a live axle on leaf springs behind.

assemblies.label: Wheels and brakes
assemblies.note: Four 265/70 R16 tyres on steel wheels and a fifth under the bed; vented discs and callipers in front, drums behind.

assemblies.label: Engine
assemblies.note: A 2.5 L four-cylinder turbo-diesel under the bonnet, 75 kW and 240 N·m.

assemblies.label: Gearbox and drive
assemblies.note: The clutch, the 5-speed gearbox, the two-piece propshaft and the rear axle’s crown wheel and pinion.

assemblies.label: Cooling, fuel and power
assemblies.note: The radiator in the nose, the battery and the air filter beside the engine, the fuel tank under the cab, the exhaust.

assemblies.label: Cab
assemblies.note: The steel cab on its rubber mounts: its sides, nose, bonnet, roof and back wall, the floor, the glass, the lights and bumpers.

assemblies.label: Doors
assemblies.note: Four doors, each on two hinges at its front edge.

assemblies.label: Seats and dashboard
assemblies.note: The dashboard and its gauges, the steering wheel and pedals, the console and the lever, two seats in front and a bench for three behind.

assemblies.label: Bed and tailgate
assemblies.note: The steel bed behind the cab on its own mounts: its floor, its double-walled sides and wheel tubs, the tailgate on its hinges and check cables.

assemblies.label: Power Cube: Frame
assemblies.note: A 27" cube: two 4×4 tube skids carry everything and take the forks; 2×2 angle posts and rails close it; the quick-attach plates on its back couple it to a machine.

assemblies.label: Power Cube: Engine
assemblies.note: An 810 cc air-cooled 90° V-twin, 28 hp at 3,600 rpm, electric start: its crank turns the pump through the coupling behind it.

assemblies.label: Power Cube: Hydraulics
assemblies.note: The gear pump on the engine’s shaft, the 7-gallon reservoir over it, the relief valve and gauge, the six-tube cooler, the return filter and the two quick couplers on the back.

assemblies.label: Power Cube: Fuel and controls
assemblies.note: The 7-gallon fuel tank on top, the 12 V battery, and the panel on the front corner with the key, choke and throttle.

parts.label: Ladder frame
parts.what: Two boxed steel rails the length of the pickup, low under the cab and kicked up over the rear axle so it can rise under the bed, joined by crossmembers; the cab and the bed sit on it on rubber mounts, the engine between its rails. A dropped crossmember carries the front suspension, another the gearbox’s tail, and the hitch’s receiver is welded to the last.

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, front left
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road and steers with the knuckle (shown turning 10 times slower).
parts.drive: The road; steered by the knuckle

parts.label: Brake disc, front left
parts.what: A vented cast-iron disc bolted to the hub between it and the wheel: the calliper squeezes it, and its vanes pump air through it to carry the heat away.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; the calliper stops it

parts.label: Brake calliper, front left
parts.what: A floating calliper over the disc’s back edge: the brake fluid pushes its piston, which presses the inner pad on the disc and pulls the outer pad on from the other side.

parts.label: Steering knuckle, front left
parts.what: The cast upright between the two wishbones’ ball joints: it carries the hub’s bearings on its spindle, the calliper on its bracket, and turns about the line through its ball joints (the kingpin axis) when the tie rod pulls its steering arm.
parts.moves: Steers about its ball joints; rides up and down with the wheel.
parts.drive: The tie rod, from the steering

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, front right
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road and steers with the knuckle (shown turning 10 times slower).
parts.drive: The road; its brake stops it

parts.label: Brake disc, front right
parts.what: A vented cast-iron disc bolted to the hub between it and the wheel: the calliper squeezes it, and its vanes pump air through it to carry the heat away.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; the calliper stops it

parts.label: Brake calliper, front right
parts.what: A floating calliper over the disc’s back edge: the brake fluid pushes its piston, which presses the inner pad on the disc and pulls the outer pad on from the other side.

parts.label: Steering knuckle, front right
parts.what: The cast upright between the two wishbones’ ball joints: it carries the hub’s bearings on its spindle, the calliper on its bracket, and turns about the line through its ball joints (the kingpin axis) when the tie rod pulls its steering arm.
parts.moves: Steers about its ball joints; rides up and down with the wheel.
parts.drive: The tie rod, from the steering

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, rear left
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).

parts.label: Brake drum, rear left
parts.what: A finned cast-iron drum on the hub: two shoes inside it, pushed out by the wheel cylinder, rub on its inner face. Cheap, sealed from the dust and good for a handbrake.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; its shoes stop it

parts.label: Backing plate, rear left
parts.what: The pressed-steel plate that closes the drum: it carries the two shoes, their springs, the wheel cylinder and the handbrake’s lever, bolted to the axle’s end.

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, rear right
parts.what: A 265/70 R16 tyre on a pressed-steel 16" rim, held on the hub by 6 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).

parts.label: Brake drum, rear right
parts.what: A finned cast-iron drum on the hub: two shoes inside it, pushed out by the wheel cylinder, rub on its inner face. Cheap, sealed from the dust and good for a handbrake.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; its shoes stop it

parts.label: Backing plate, rear right
parts.what: The pressed-steel plate that closes the drum: it carries the two shoes, their springs, the wheel cylinder and the handbrake’s lever, bolted to the axle’s end.

parts.label: Spare wheel
parts.what: A fifth wheel and tyre hung flat under the back of the bed on a cable: a crank through the bumper winds it down.

parts.label: Upper wishbone, front left
parts.what: A pressed and welded A-arm from two rubber bushes on the frame to the knuckle’s upper ball joint: with the lower arm it holds the wheel upright as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks on its springs.

parts.label: Lower wishbone, front left
parts.what: The longer, stronger lower A-arm: it carries the coil spring’s load from the knuckle’s lower ball joint to the frame and takes the braking forces.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks.

parts.label: Coil spring and damper, front left
parts.what: A coil spring round a telescopic damper from the lower arm up to its tower on the frame: the spring carries the body, the damper’s oil forced through its valves stops it bouncing.
parts.moves: Shortens as the load or the climb presses the front down; lengthens as it lifts.
parts.drive: The road, through the lower arm

parts.label: Tie rod, front left
parts.what: From the steering rack’s end to the knuckle’s steering arm: as the rack slides, it pushes or pulls the arm and turns the wheel about its ball joints. Its threaded end sets the toe.
parts.moves: Follows the rack and the wheel.

parts.label: Upper wishbone, front right
parts.what: A pressed and welded A-arm from two rubber bushes on the frame to the knuckle’s upper ball joint: with the lower arm it holds the wheel upright as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks on its springs.

parts.label: Lower wishbone, front right
parts.what: The longer, stronger lower A-arm: it carries the coil spring’s load from the knuckle’s lower ball joint to the frame and takes the braking forces.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks.

parts.label: Coil spring and damper, front right
parts.what: A coil spring round a telescopic damper from the lower arm up to its tower on the frame: the spring carries the body, the damper’s oil forced through its valves stops it bouncing.
parts.moves: Shortens as the load or the climb presses the front down; lengthens as it lifts.
parts.drive: The road, through the lower arm

parts.label: Tie rod, front right
parts.what: From the steering rack’s end to the knuckle’s steering arm: as the rack slides, it pushes or pulls the arm and turns the wheel about its ball joints. Its threaded end sets the toe.
parts.moves: Follows the rack and the wheel.

parts.label: Steering rack
parts.what: A rack-and-pinion box across the front: the steering wheel’s shaft turns the pinion, the pinion slides the toothed rack sideways, the rack pushes and pulls the tie rods.
parts.moves: The rack slides as the wheel is turned (held straight here).
parts.drive: The steering wheel, through its shaft and universal joints

parts.label: Rear axle housing
parts.what: The banjo housing: a pressed-steel bowl round the differential with a tube out to each wheel, its spring seats welded on. It carries the vehicle’s rear and its load straight to the wheels.

parts.label: Crown wheel, pinion and half-shafts
parts.what: The propshaft turns the pinion, the pinion turns the crown wheel 4.1 times slower and a right angle round; the differential’s gears on the crown wheel share its torque between the half-shafts, letting the outer wheel turn faster in a bend.
parts.moves: The pinion turns with the propshaft, the crown wheel and half-shafts with the wheels (shown slowed).

parts.label: Leaf springs and U-bolts
parts.what: Two packs of 5 steel leaves, each clamped to the axle by two U-bolts, its front eye on a hanger, its back eye on a swinging shackle: they carry the load and locate the axle. They flatten as the load grows.
parts.moves: Flatten as the body sinks onto the axle, arch again as it lifts.

parts.label: Spring hangers and shackles
parts.what: Under the frame: a fixed hanger for each spring’s front eye and a swinging shackle for its back eye, so the leaves can lengthen as they flatten.

parts.label: Rear dampers
parts.what: Telescopic dampers from the axle up to the frame, leaning in: oil forced through their valves turns the body’s bounce into heat.
parts.moves: Shorten as the body sinks, lengthen as it lifts.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cylinder block, 2.5 L turbo-diesel
parts.what: The cast-iron block: four 93 mm bores bored through its deck, water round them, the crankcase under them with five bulkheads that carry the crankshaft’s main bearings. Everything else on the engine bolts to it.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cylinder head
parts.what: The aluminium head closing the bores: its ports, the valves’ seats and guides, the camshaft’s bearings and the injectors’ wells; held down on its gasket by ten long bolts.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cam cover
parts.what: The pressed cover over the camshaft and valves, keeping their oil in; its cap is where the oil goes in.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Camshaft and valves
parts.what: One overhead camshaft, turned by the timing belt at half the crank’s speed: its lobes push the eight valves open through their buckets, their springs close them.
parts.moves: Turns at half the crank’s speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.what: The forged crankshaft on its five main bearings: its four pins, two up and two down, turn the pistons’ push into torque; the counterweights opposite them balance it.
parts.moves: Turns at the engine’s speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Pistons
parts.what: Four cast-aluminium pistons, the combustion bowl in each crown where the fuel is sprayed, three rings sealing them in their bores; each pushed down by its burning charge.
parts.moves: Up and down their bores (shown 40 times slower).
parts.drive: The burning charge; they drive the rods

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Connecting rods
parts.what: Forged steel I-section rods from each piston’s pin to its crank pin, their big ends split and bolted round the pins on shell bearings.
parts.moves: Swing and slide with the pistons.
parts.drive: The pistons; they drive the crankshaft

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Flywheel
parts.what: A heavy steel disc on the crank’s back end: it carries the engine through the strokes between firings and is the clutch’s friction face; the starter turns its ring gear.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Clutch
parts.what: A friction disc pressed against the flywheel by the cover’s diaphragm spring: it passes the engine’s torque to the gearbox, and slips to let the vehicle pull away.
parts.moves: Turns with the flywheel; slips while it pulls away.
parts.drive: The pedal, through its cable and release bearing

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Sump
parts.what: The pressed-steel oil pan under the crankcase, deep at one end where the pump’s pickup draws the oil; its drain plug at the bottom.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Timing belt and cover
parts.what: A toothed belt from the crank to the camshaft and the injection pump, both turning at half the crank’s speed so each valve and each squirt of fuel comes at its stroke; under its plastic cover.
parts.moves: The belt runs round its three sprockets.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Accessory belt and water pump
parts.what: A V-belt from the crank’s pulley (its damper behind) round the water pump’s and the alternator’s: the pump drives the coolant through the block, the head and the radiator.
parts.moves: The belt and pulleys turn with the engine.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Alternator
parts.what: Turned by the belt at about 2.5 times the crank’s speed, it charges the battery and runs the lights.
parts.moves: Its rotor and pulley turn with the belt.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Fan and viscous coupling
parts.what: Seven plastic blades on the water pump’s hub through a viscous coupling: it pulls air through the radiator, slipping when the air is cool.
parts.moves: Turns with the water pump.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Injection pump, lines and injectors
parts.what: The distributor pump, turned by the timing belt, meters the fuel and squeezes it to some 300 bar into each injector in turn through its own steel line, at the moment its piston comes up on compression; the glow plugs on the other side warm the chambers for a cold start.
parts.moves: Its shaft turns at half the crank’s speed.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Intake manifold
parts.what: The cast-aluminium manifold that shares the air from the filter among the four inlet ports.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Exhaust manifold and turbocharger
parts.what: The cast-iron manifold gathers the four cylinders’ gas into the turbocharger’s turbine; its compressor on the same shaft pushes the air into the intake at up to 0.9 bar.
parts.moves: The turbo’s shaft spins at up to 150,000 rpm (not shown turning).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Oil filter and dipstick
parts.what: A spin-on full-flow filter that the oil pump pushes all the oil through before the bearings; the dipstick to check its level.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Starter motor
parts.what: A 12 V motor on the bellhousing’s flange: its solenoid throws its pinion into the flywheel’s ring gear and it spins the engine to start it.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Engine and gearbox mounts
parts.what: Rubber blocks between the engine’s brackets and the frame, and under the gearbox’s tail: they carry its weight and its torque and keep its shake out of the body.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Bellhousing
parts.what: The cast-aluminium bell bolted to the block’s back face round the flywheel and clutch, carrying the gearbox and the starter.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Gearbox, 5 speeds
parts.what: A 5-speed manual gearbox: the input shaft from the clutch drives the layshaft below it, whose gears turn the gears riding free on the output shaft; the lever slides a synchro collar to lock one of them to the shaft (top gear locks the input to the output straight).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Shafts and gears
parts.what: Inside the case: the input shaft and its gear, the layshaft and its cluster, the output shaft with the gears that ride on it, all in constant mesh; the synchro collars between them.
parts.moves: The shafts and gears turn (shown 40 times slower).
specs: Constant, helical in the case [simplified straight here]

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Gear lever
parts.what: The lever and its rod into the gearbox’s selector: across to pick a gate, forward and back to choose a gear.
parts.moves: Moved by hand; the solver changes gear by itself.

parts.label: Propshaft (two pieces)
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: Two thin-walled steel tubes from the gearbox to the axle, joined over a rubber-mounted centre bearing under the floor, a universal joint at each end of each to follow the axle as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Turns at the gearbox’s output speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.label: Centre bearing bracket
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: A pressed-steel bracket under the cab’s floor holding the propshaft’s centre bearing in its rubber.

parts.label: Radiator and shroud
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: In the nose behind the grille: the engine’s coolant runs down through the radiator’s finned tubes and gives its heat to the air the road and the engine’s fan pull through it; the shroud round the fan makes it pull through all of the core.
specs: About a third of the fuel’s heat at full load

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: The starting battery on its tray over the right front wheel: it cranks the engine and heats the glow plugs; the alternator charges it.

parts.label: Air filter and intake
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: The engine breathes through a paper element in this box over the left front wheel, then through a duct to the turbocharger’s compressor.

parts.label: Fuel tank
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: A 76 L pressed-steel tank outside the right rail under the cab’s back, hung on two straps; its filler neck runs up to the cap on the bed’s side.

parts.label: Exhaust and silencer
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: From the turbocharger down and back under the cab through the silencer, over the axle and out under the back on the right, hung on rubber loops.

parts.label: Cab sides and front wings
parts.what: The two pressed-steel sides of the cab and its front wings in one: the four door openings, the pillars between them, the front wheels’ arches cut in; the wheel housings and inner wings inside.

parts.label: Nose, roof and back wall
parts.what: The cab’s ends and top: the nose with the grille’s opening, the cowl under the windscreen, the windscreen’s frame, the roof, and the back wall with its window; every edge rounded onto the sides.

parts.label: Bonnet
parts.what: The steel bonnet over the engine, hinged at its back edge under the windscreen, a stay to hold it up; its rounded edges meet the wings.

parts.label: Windscreen and back window
parts.what: The laminated windscreen raked back over the bonnet, and the toughened window in the cab’s back wall.

parts.label: Floor, firewall and lining
parts.what: The cab’s steel floor on the frame’s mounts, a tunnel down its middle over the gearbox and the propshaft, the firewall between the engine and the cab, a rubber mat over the floor; the headlining under the roof and the trim on the back wall.

parts.label: Bumpers, plates and mounts
parts.what: A steel bumper in front, a step bumper behind with the hitch’s receiver through it, both on brackets to the frame; the number plates (blank); the cab’s rubber mounts on the frame’s outriggers.

parts.label: Headlights and grille
parts.what: Two headlights with their indicators beside them in the nose, the grille between them that lets the air to the radiator, the side repeaters on the wings.

parts.label: Wipers
parts.what: Two wipers parked at the windscreen’s foot, driven by one motor under the cowl.

parts.label: Front door, left (the driver’s)
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles, its mirror on its front corner. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Front door, right
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles, its mirror on its front corner. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Rear door, left
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Rear door, right
parts.what: A hinged steel door, its window wound down into it by a handle inside, its card, armrest and handles. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Front seats
parts.what: The driver’s seat and the passenger’s, on runners to slide them, their backs raked, a headrest on each.

parts.label: Rear bench
parts.what: A bench for three across the back of the cab, upright against its back wall.

parts.label: Dashboard and gauges
parts.what: The moulded dashboard under the windscreen: the speedometer and the rev counter in their binnacle before the driver, the radio and the heater’s controls in the middle, four vents, the glovebox before the passenger.
parts.moves: Its needles show the speed and the engine’s revs.
specs: Speed to 180 km/h, revs to 5,000 rpm

parts.label: Steering wheel and column
parts.what: The wheel on its column through the dashboard to the firewall, where a shaft with two universal joints runs down past the engine to the rack.
parts.moves: Turned by the driver (held straight here).

parts.label: Pedals, console and handbrake
parts.what: Clutch, brake and accelerator hanging from under the dashboard; the console over the tunnel between the front seats with the gear lever through it and the handbrake beside it, which pulls the rear drums’ shoes by cable.

parts.label: Bed sides and front wall
parts.what: The bed’s double walls: the painted outer skins with the rear wheels’ arches cut in, the inner walls the load rubs against, the caps along their tops, the front wall behind the cab, the back posts carrying the lights; the wheel housings under the floor and the tubs over them.

parts.label: Bed floor
parts.what: The bed’s floor: a ribbed steel sheet on four bearers across the frame’s rails, coated against wear; eight hooks along its edges to tie the load down. What is put on the bed stands on it.

parts.label: Tail lights
parts.what: The tail, brake, indicator and reversing lights on the bed’s back posts.

parts.label: Tailgate
parts.what: The bed’s back wall on two hinges along its bottom edge: unlatched by its handle it drops back to lie level with the floor, held there by two steel check cables, to load the bed or to carry something longer than it.
parts.moves: Drops 90° on its hinges.

parts.label: Tailgate sill and hinges
parts.what: The sill along the bed’s back edge that the tailgate’s hinge pins turn in.

parts.label: Base skids (4×4 tube)
parts.what: Two 4×4 steel tubes front to back under the cube: the strong frame of 7s that the engine, pump and tanks bolt to, and that takes a forklift’s forks, the lifting pins or another cube stacked on it.

parts.label: Cross tubes (2×2)
parts.what: Two 2×2 tubes welded between the skids at front and back, squaring the base.

parts.label: Corner posts (2×2 angle)
parts.what: Four corner posts of 1/4" × 2" × 2" angle make the cage: they guard the engine, carry the rails and give hand-holds to lift it by.

parts.label: Top rails (2×2 angle)
parts.what: Four rails round the top of the cage: OSE’s frame cuts its members 29", 27" and 24" long. The lifting eyes and the fuel tank’s rails hang on them.

parts.label: Fuel tank rails
parts.what: Two angles across the cage under the top, the fuel tank resting on them, clear of the engine’s air cleaner.

parts.label: Engine mount plate
parts.what: A 1/2" plate across the skids: the engine’s base bolts to it, and the pump’s bracket behind, so their shafts stay on one line.
specs: 8" × 15½" (203 × 394 mm), here one piece with the pump’s [inferred]

parts.label: Quick-attach plates and receiver
parts.what: How the cube is coupled to a machine: plates across its back with a 4×8 receiver tube between them, so it slides onto the machine’s mount and is pinned, and comes off again in minutes for the next machine.

parts.label: Lifting eyes
parts.what: Two eyes welded on the top rails: at about 181 kg the cube is lifted on and off a machine by the loader, a hoist or two people with a bar.

parts.label: Crankcase
parts.what: The engine’s cast block: it carries the crankshaft in its two main bearings, the camshaft and the governor, holds the oil in its sump, and bolts to the plate by its flange.

parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.what: One forged crank for both cylinders: their two rods share one pin, the counterweights balance them, its front end carries the flywheel and its back end drives the pump.
parts.moves: Turns at engine speed (shown slowed 40 times).
parts.drive: The pistons, through the rods; it drives the pump

parts.label: Cylinder, left
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V: a cast-iron liner the piston runs in, cast into square aluminium fins that the flywheel’s fan blows air over.

parts.label: Cylinder head, left
parts.what: The overhead-valve head: its inlet and exhaust valves under the rocker cover, the combustion chamber over the piston, and the spark plug in its front.

parts.label: Spark plug and lead, left
parts.what: The plug in the head, its boot and the lead to its ignition coil at the flywheel: a spark each turn, fired by the flywheel’s magnet.

parts.label: Piston, left
parts.what: An aluminium piston with two compression rings and an oil ring, on a hardened pin: the burning charge pushes it down 405 cm³ a stroke.
parts.moves: Up and down its cylinder, twice a turn of the crank for its four strokes.
parts.drive: The burning charge; it turns the crank through its rod

parts.label: Connecting rod, left
parts.what: The forged rod from the piston’s pin to the crank’s pin, beside its twin on the same pin.
parts.moves: Swings and slides with the crank.

parts.label: Cylinder, right
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V: a cast-iron liner the piston runs in, cast into square aluminium fins that the flywheel’s fan blows air over.

parts.label: Cylinder head, right
parts.what: The overhead-valve head: its inlet and exhaust valves under the rocker cover, the combustion chamber over the piston, and the spark plug in its front.

parts.label: Spark plug and lead, right
parts.what: The plug in the head, its boot and the lead to its ignition coil at the flywheel: a spark each turn, fired by the flywheel’s magnet.

parts.label: Piston, right
parts.what: An aluminium piston with two compression rings and an oil ring, on a hardened pin: the burning charge pushes it down 405 cm³ a stroke.
parts.moves: Up and down its cylinder, twice a turn of the crank for its four strokes.
parts.drive: The burning charge; it turns the crank through its rod

parts.label: Connecting rod, right
parts.what: The forged rod from the piston’s pin to the crank’s pin, beside its twin on the same pin.
parts.moves: Swings and slides with the crank.

parts.label: Flywheel, fan and ring gear
parts.what: Cast iron at the crank’s front: its weight smooths the twin’s firing, its magnets fire the plugs and charge the battery, its vanes are the cooling fan, and its ring gear takes the starter.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft (shown slowed 40 times).

parts.label: Rotating screen
parts.what: The perforated disc on the flywheel’s face: it turns with it and flings off grass and chaff before the fan draws its air in.
parts.moves: Turns with the flywheel.

parts.label: Blower housing
parts.what: The pressed-steel shroud over the flywheel, ducting its fan’s air back over both cylinders’ fins.

parts.label: Carburettor and intake
parts.what: In the V: the carburettor mixes petrol into the air the cleaner gives it, its throttle opened by the governor, and the manifold carries the charge to both heads.
parts.moves: Its throttle plate opens and closes with the governor.

parts.label: Air cleaner
parts.what: Over the V: a pleated paper element in a plastic cover. Every litre of air the engine breathes, about 45 litres a second at full speed, is cleaned here first.

parts.label: Muffler and exhaust
parts.what: Both exhausts into one can on the cube’s left side, the right one crossing behind the cylinders; it blows out forward, away from the couplers.

parts.label: Electric starter
parts.what: The 12 V starter whose pinion meshes with the flywheel’s ring gear while the key is held to START.
parts.moves: Spins only while starting.

parts.label: Oil filter and dipstick
parts.what: The engine’s full-pressure lubrication: a spin-on filter low on its right side, and the dipstick tube to fill and check the oil.

parts.label: Ignition coils
parts.what: One coil beside the flywheel’s rim for each plug: its magnet sweeping past them makes the spark, no battery needed.

parts.label: Governor and linkage
parts.what: Flyweights inside the crankcase push a lever out as the speed rises; its rod closes the throttle, so the engine holds its set speed whatever the pump asks, drooping a little under load.
parts.moves: Opens and closes the throttle.

parts.label: Shaft coupling
parts.what: Not a bought jaw coupling: OSE cut two coupling halves and welded them into one sleeve, keyed and set-screwed onto the engine’s shaft, splined onto the pump’s.
parts.moves: Turns with the engine (shown slowed).
parts.drive: The crankshaft; it drives the pump

parts.label: Pump bracket
parts.what: An upright plate on the engine plate holding the pump’s SAE-A flange square to the engine, so the two shafts stay on one line.
specs: SAE A: Ø 82.55 mm pilot, 2 bolts on 106.4 mm

parts.label: Hydraulic gear pump
parts.what: A fixed-displacement external gear pump: two gears mesh and carry oil round the outside of their teeth from the suction port to the pressure port, about a cubic inch every turn. This flow is everything the machine it is coupled to can do.
parts.moves: Its gears turn with the engine.
specs: 15.2 gpm (57.5 L/min) at 3,600 rpm, less its slip

parts.label: Pump gears
parts.what: The drive gear on the pump’s shaft and the idler it turns: oil trapped between their teeth and the housing is carried round the outside from suction to pressure, and the meshing teeth push it out.
parts.moves: Turn against each other at engine speed.
specs: 2π m² z b ≈ 16 cm³ a turn

parts.label: Hydraulic reservoir
parts.what: The oil tank over the pump, removable for cleaning: the pump draws through a strainer at its bottom, the returns come in at its top through the filter, and a baffle between them makes the oil settle and let go of its air before it is drawn again.

parts.label: Hydraulic oil
parts.what: About 21 L of ISO VG 46 anti-wear oil at its working level: it carries the power out to the machine and back, lubricates the pump and takes away the heat of every loss.

parts.label: Baffle and suction strainer
parts.what: A plate across the tank between the return and the suction, and a brass mesh strainer on the suction outlet at its bottom: the pump never draws air or grit.

parts.label: Suction hose
parts.what: The wide soft line from the tank’s strainer down to the pump’s inlet: wide, so the pump never starves and cavitates.

parts.label: Relief valve
parts.what: Added in October 2014: a spring-loaded poppet that opens back to the tank when the pressure reaches its setting, so nothing bursts when a cylinder bottoms out or a wheel stalls. All the power it dumps becomes heat in the oil.
parts.moves: Its poppet lifts only at its setting.

parts.label: Pressure hoses
parts.what: Two-wire braided hoses from the pump to the relief valve and on to the pressure coupler, every power stroke of the machine’s cylinders coming through them.

parts.label: Pressure gauge
parts.what: A liquid-filled gauge on the pressure line, added in April 2015: the operator sees at a glance how hard the cube is working.
parts.moves: Its needle swings with the pressure.

parts.label: Quick couplers
parts.what: The cube’s whole connection to a machine: the pressure coupler (red cap) and the return coupler (blue) on its back. Push the machine’s hoses on and the cube drives it; pull them off and it is free for the next one.

parts.label: Return hoses
parts.what: From the return coupler through the cooler and the filter back into the tank: everything the machine sends back.

parts.label: Oil cooler (six tubes)
parts.what: The 7s cooler on the cube’s right side: the returning oil runs through six finned tubes before the filter, giving the heat of every loss to the air its fan pulls through.

parts.label: Cooler fan
parts.what: The 12 V fan pulling air through the cooler’s fins into the cube.
parts.moves: Turns while the engine runs.

parts.label: Return filter
parts.what: A spin-on filter on the tank’s top where the return enters it: everything that comes back from the machine passes through it.

parts.label: Filler and breather cap
parts.what: Where the tank is filled, and how it breathes as the machine’s cylinders draw oil out and give it back.

parts.label: Sight gauge
parts.what: A window on the tank’s back above the strainer: the oil’s level and colour at a glance.

parts.label: Fuel tank
parts.what: The removable petrol tank on top of the cube, over the engine: lift it off to fill it away from the machine. Moulded of natural polyethylene, so the petrol’s level shows through its wall.

parts.label: Petrol
parts.what: The fuel at 70 % of the tank: what the engine burns, about 0.37 kg for every kWh it makes at full load.

parts.label: Fuel line and shut-off
parts.what: From the tank’s outlet down the front through a shut-off valve and an inline filter to the carburettor.

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.what: The cube’s own 12 V battery in the front corner: it cranks the starter, runs the cooler fan and the machine’s valves; the flywheel alternator charges it.

parts.label: Battery cables
parts.what: The red cable from the battery across the front to the starter’s solenoid, the black to the frame.

parts.label: Control panel
parts.what: On the front corner post: the key switch (off, run, start), the choke knob, the throttle lever that sets the governor’s speed, and an hour meter. The cube is started here and left running; the machine’s valves do the rest.
parts.moves: Key, choke and throttle are worked by hand.

parts.label: Ratchet straps
parts.what: Two 25 mm ratchet straps over the Power Cube’s frame from the bed’s hooks: they hold its 181 kg down on the floor through braking, bends and bumps.

assemblies.label: Frame
assemblies.note: A 27" cube: two 4×4 tube skids carry everything and take the lifting pins; 2×2 angle posts and top rails close it, and its quick-attach plate couples it to a machine.

assemblies.label: Engine
