assemblies.label: Hydraulics
assemblies.note: The gear pump on the engine’s shaft, the 7-gallon reservoir, the relief valve and gauge, the six-tube cooler, the return filter and the two quick couplers out.

assemblies.label: Fuel and controls
assemblies.note: The removable 7-gallon fuel tank, the 12 V battery and the panel with the key, the choke and the throttle.

parts.label: Power Cube base skids (4×4 tube)
parts.what: Two 4×4 steel tubes front to back under the cube: the “strong structural frame” of 7s that the engine, pump and tanks bolt to, and that takes the forks, the lifting pins or another cube stacked on it.

parts.label: Power Cube posts and top rails (2×2 angle)
parts.what: Four corner posts and four top rails of 1/4" × 2" × 2" angle make the cube’s cage: they guard the engine, carry the fuel tank and give hand-holds to lift it by. OSE’s frame page cuts its members 29", 27" and 24" long.

parts.label: Power Cube quick-attach plate
parts.what: How the cube is coupled to a machine: plates across its back with a 4×8 receiver tube between them, so it slides onto the machine’s mount and is pinned, and comes off again in minutes for the next machine. Several cubes can be strung together for more power.

parts.label: Power Cube lifting eyes
parts.what: Two eyes on the top rails: at about 181 kg the cube is lifted on and off a machine by the loader, a hoist or two people with a bar.

parts.label: Engine mount plate
parts.what: The plate the engine’s base bolts to, itself bolted across the skids: it holds the engine’s shaft exactly in line with the pump’s.

parts.label: Engine crankcase
parts.what: The 28 hp Briggs & Stratton V-twin’s crankcase: crankshaft, camshaft, the oil sump and the governor that holds it at its speed. The crankshaft runs fore and aft: the flywheel at the front, the pump at the back.
parts.moves: The crankshaft inside turns at engine speed.
specs: Briggs & Stratton 28 hp (20.9 kW) V-twin, air-cooled

parts.label: Engine cylinder and head, left
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V-twin: a finned air-cooled cylinder and its overhead-valve head. The flywheel’s fan pushes air through the shroud and over these fins.
parts.moves: Its piston runs up and down inside, twice per two turns of the crank.

parts.label: Engine cylinder and head, right
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V-twin: a finned air-cooled cylinder and its overhead-valve head. The flywheel’s fan pushes air through the shroud and over these fins.
parts.moves: Its piston runs up and down inside, twice per two turns of the crank.

parts.label: Blower housing
parts.what: The shroud over the flywheel, ducting its fan’s air back over both cylinders.

parts.label: Flywheel and fan screen
parts.what: The flywheel at the crank’s front: its weight smooths the twin’s firing, its magnets fire the plugs and charge the battery, its vanes are the cooling fan.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft (shown slowed: really 60 turns a second).

parts.label: Air cleaner
parts.what: The paper element in the V between the cylinders: every litre of air the engine breathes is cleaned here first.

parts.label: Muffler
parts.what: The Briggs & Stratton muffler behind the cylinders, collecting both exhausts into one can and blowing out to the side.

parts.label: Electric starter
parts.what: The 12 V starter whose pinion meshes with the flywheel’s ring gear while the key is held to START.
parts.moves: Spins only while starting.

parts.label: Shaft coupling
parts.what: Not a bought jaw coupling: OSE cut two coupling halves and welded them into one sleeve, keyed and set-screwed to the engine’s shaft, splined onto the pump’s 3/4" shaft.
parts.moves: Turns with the engine (shown slowed).
parts.drive: The crankshaft; it drives the pump

parts.label: Pump mount
parts.what: A plate on the engine plate holding the pump’s SAE-A flange square to the engine, its two bolts on 4.19" centres, so the shafts stay in line.

parts.label: Hydraulic gear pump
parts.what: A fixed-displacement gear pump: two gears mesh and carry oil from the suction port round to the pressure port — about a cubic inch every turn, 15 gallons a minute at engine speed. This flow is everything the machine it is coupled to can do.
parts.moves: Its gears turn with the engine.

parts.label: Hydraulic reservoir (7 gal)
parts.what: The oil tank across the back of the cube, removable for cleaning. The pump draws through a strainer at its bottom; returns come back in at its top, where the oil settles and lets go of its air. Earlier cubes used their tanks as members of the frame.

parts.label: Suction strainer and line
parts.what: A mesh strainer inside the reservoir’s outlet and the wide soft line down to the pump’s inlet: wide so the pump never starves and cavitates.

parts.label: Relief valve
parts.what: Added to the cube in October 2014: a spring-loaded valve that dumps the pump’s flow back to the tank when the pressure reaches its setting, so nothing bursts when a cylinder bottoms out or a wheel stalls.
parts.moves: Its poppet lifts only at its setting.

parts.label: Pressure gauge
parts.what: A liquid-filled gauge on the pressure line, added in April 2015: the operator sees at a glance how hard the cube is working.

parts.label: Oil cooler (six tubes)
parts.what: v15.6’s cooler on the cube’s side: the returning oil runs through six finned tubes before the filter, giving the heat of every relief and orifice to the air.

parts.label: Cooler fan
parts.what: The 12 V fan pulling air through the cooler’s tubes.
parts.moves: Turns while the engine runs (shown slowed).

parts.label: Return filter
parts.what: A spin-on filter on the return line where it enters the reservoir: everything that comes back from the machine passes through it.

parts.label: Filler and breather cap
parts.what: Where the reservoir is filled, and how it breathes as the machine’s cylinders draw oil out and give it back.

parts.label: Quick couplers (pressure and return)
parts.what: The cube’s whole connection to a machine: a pressure coupler and a return coupler on its back. Push the machine’s hoses on and the cube drives it; pull them off and it is free for the next one.

parts.label: Fuel tank (7 gal)
parts.what: The removable petrol tank on top of the cube, over the engine: lift it off to fill it away from the machine.

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.what: The cube’s own 12 V battery beside the engine: it cranks the starter, runs the cooler fan and the machine’s valves; the flywheel alternator charges it.

parts.label: Control panel
parts.what: On the front corner post: the key switch (off, run, start), the choke and the throttle. The cube is started here and left running; the machine’s valves do the rest.
parts.moves: Key, choke and throttle are worked by hand.

parts.drive: The crankshaft; it drives the rotor

parts.label: Alternator adapter (bell housing)
parts.what: An SAE bell housing bolted to the engine’s face and the alternator’s flange: it holds the two shafts in line, as the pump mount did.

parts.label: Brushless alternator
parts.what: A single-bearing, brushless synchronous alternator: its rotor turns inside the stator’s copper windings and gives alternating current at the engine’s governed speed. The 28 hp twin carries about 15 kVA of it.
parts.moves: Its rotor turns with the engine.
specs: 400 V three-phase and 230 V, 50 Hz at 3,000 rpm (60 Hz at 3,600)
Its own fan, on the rotor

parts.label: Alternator foot
parts.what: A steel foot under the alternator’s end bell, bolted to the frame’s back cross member on rubber mounts; its flange end hangs on the engine.

parts.label: Control box (regulator and breakers)
parts.what: The box on the cube’s back: the automatic voltage regulator that holds the voltage steady as loads come and go, the main breaker, an earth-leakage breaker, an hour meter and a voltmeter.

parts.label: Sockets
parts.what: What the cube gives out: a red three-phase socket for the village grid or a workshop, and two blue 230 V sockets for a home or tools, each under its spring lid.

parts.label: Alternator cable
parts.what: The armoured cable from the alternator’s terminal box to the control box and sockets.

parts.label: Fuel tank (7 gal)
parts.what: The removable petrol tank on top of the cube, over the engine: lift it off to fill it away from the machine.

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.what: The cube’s own 12 V battery beside the engine: it cranks the starter, runs the cooler fan and the machine’s valves; the flywheel alternator charges it.

parts.label: Control panel
parts.what: On the front corner post: the key switch (off, run, start), the choke and the throttle. The cube is started here and left running; the machine’s valves do the rest.
parts.moves: Key, choke and throttle are worked by hand.

steps: Cut, drill and bolt the frame: skids, posts, top rails, quick-attach plate
Bolt in the engine on its mount plate
Flange the alternator to the engine on its coupling; fit its feet, the control box, the sockets and the cable

b9f17a791526e7648724032b4c9b04798a559a54.label: Power Cube: VII / 7s
b9f17a791526e7648724032b4c9b04798a559a54.note: as at v2: one rigged mesh in flat colours, its parts named

assemblies.label: Frame
assemblies.note: A 27" cube: two 4×4 tube skids carry everything and take the lifting pins; 2×2 angle posts and top rails close it, and its quick-attach plate couples it to a machine.

assemblies.label: Engine
assemblies.note: A 28 hp Briggs & Stratton air-cooled V-twin with electric start, on its mount plate: the prime mover of every machine the cube is coupled to.

assemblies.label: Hydraulics
assemblies.note: The gear pump on the engine’s shaft, the 7-gallon reservoir, the relief valve and gauge, the six-tube cooler, the return filter and the two quick couplers out.

assemblies.label: Fuel and controls
assemblies.note: The removable 7-gallon fuel tank, the 12 V battery and the panel with the key, the choke and the throttle.

parts.label: Power Cube base skids (4×4 tube)
parts.what: Two 4×4 steel tubes front to back under the cube: the “strong structural frame” of 7s that the engine, pump and tanks bolt to, and that takes the forks, the lifting pins or another cube stacked on it.

parts.label: Power Cube posts and top rails (2×2 angle)
parts.what: Four corner posts and four top rails of 1/4" × 2" × 2" angle make the cube’s cage: they guard the engine, carry the fuel tank and give hand-holds to lift it by. OSE’s frame page cuts its members 29", 27" and 24" long.

parts.label: Power Cube quick-attach plate
parts.what: How the cube is coupled to a machine: plates across its back with a 4×8 receiver tube between them, so it slides onto the machine’s mount and is pinned, and comes off again in minutes for the next machine. Several cubes can be strung together for more power.

parts.label: Power Cube lifting eyes
parts.what: Two eyes on the top rails: at about 181 kg the cube is lifted on and off a machine by the loader, a hoist or two people with a bar.

parts.label: Engine mount plate
parts.what: The plate the engine’s base bolts to, itself bolted across the skids: it holds the engine’s shaft exactly in line with the pump’s.

parts.label: Engine crankcase
parts.what: The 28 hp Briggs & Stratton V-twin’s crankcase: crankshaft, camshaft, the oil sump and the governor that holds it at its speed. The crankshaft runs fore and aft: the flywheel at the front, the pump at the back.
parts.moves: The crankshaft inside turns at engine speed.
specs: Briggs & Stratton 28 hp (20.9 kW) V-twin, air-cooled

parts.label: Engine cylinder and head, left
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V-twin: a finned air-cooled cylinder and its overhead-valve head. The flywheel’s fan pushes air through the shroud and over these fins.
parts.moves: Its piston runs up and down inside, twice per two turns of the crank.

parts.label: Engine cylinder and head, right
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V-twin: a finned air-cooled cylinder and its overhead-valve head. The flywheel’s fan pushes air through the shroud and over these fins.
parts.moves: Its piston runs up and down inside, twice per two turns of the crank.

parts.label: Blower housing
parts.what: The shroud over the flywheel, ducting its fan’s air back over both cylinders.

parts.label: Flywheel and fan screen
parts.what: The flywheel at the crank’s front: its weight smooths the twin’s firing, its magnets fire the plugs and charge the battery, its vanes are the cooling fan.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft (shown slowed: really 60 turns a second).

parts.label: Air cleaner
parts.what: The paper element in the V between the cylinders: every litre of air the engine breathes is cleaned here first.

parts.label: Muffler
parts.what: The Briggs & Stratton muffler behind the cylinders, collecting both exhausts into one can and blowing out to the side.

parts.label: Electric starter
parts.what: The 12 V starter whose pinion meshes with the flywheel’s ring gear while the key is held to START.
parts.moves: Spins only while starting.

parts.label: Shaft coupling
parts.what: Not a bought jaw coupling: OSE cut two coupling halves and welded them into one sleeve, keyed and set-screwed to the engine’s shaft, splined onto the pump’s 3/4" shaft.
parts.moves: Turns with the engine (shown slowed).
parts.drive: The crankshaft; it drives the pump

parts.label: Pump mount
parts.what: A plate on the engine plate holding the pump’s SAE-A flange square to the engine, its two bolts on 4.19" centres, so the shafts stay in line.

parts.label: Hydraulic gear pump
parts.what: A fixed-displacement gear pump: two gears mesh and carry oil from the suction port round to the pressure port — about a cubic inch every turn, 15 gallons a minute at engine speed. This flow is everything the machine it is coupled to can do.
parts.moves: Its gears turn with the engine.

parts.label: Hydraulic reservoir (7 gal)
parts.what: The oil tank across the back of the cube, removable for cleaning. The pump draws through a strainer at its bottom; returns come back in at its top, where the oil settles and lets go of its air. Earlier cubes used their tanks as members of the frame.

parts.label: Suction strainer and line
parts.what: A mesh strainer inside the reservoir’s outlet and the wide soft line down to the pump’s inlet: wide so the pump never starves and cavitates.

parts.label: Relief valve
parts.what: Added to the cube in October 2014: a spring-loaded valve that dumps the pump’s flow back to the tank when the pressure reaches its setting, so nothing bursts when a cylinder bottoms out or a wheel stalls.
parts.moves: Its poppet lifts only at its setting.

parts.label: Pressure gauge
parts.what: A liquid-filled gauge on the pressure line, added in April 2015: the operator sees at a glance how hard the cube is working.

parts.label: Oil cooler (six tubes)
parts.what: v15.6’s cooler on the cube’s side: the returning oil runs through six finned tubes before the filter, giving the heat of every relief and orifice to the air.

parts.label: Cooler fan
parts.what: The 12 V fan pulling air through the cooler’s tubes.
parts.moves: Turns while the engine runs (shown slowed).

parts.label: Return filter
parts.what: A spin-on filter on the return line where it enters the reservoir: everything that comes back from the machine passes through it.

parts.label: Filler and breather cap
parts.what: Where the reservoir is filled, and how it breathes as the machine’s cylinders draw oil out and give it back.

parts.label: Quick couplers (pressure and return)
parts.what: The cube’s whole connection to a machine: a pressure coupler and a return coupler on its back. Push the machine’s hoses on and the cube drives it; pull them off and it is free for the next one.

parts.label: Fuel tank (7 gal)
parts.what: The removable petrol tank on top of the cube, over the engine: lift it off to fill it away from the machine.

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.what: The cube’s own 12 V battery beside the engine: it cranks the starter, runs the cooler fan and the machine’s valves; the flywheel alternator charges it.

parts.label: Control panel
parts.what: On the front corner post: the key switch (off, run, start), the choke and the throttle. The cube is started here and left running; the machine’s valves do the rest.
parts.moves: Key, choke and throttle are worked by hand.

Bolt in the engine on its mount plate
Mount the pump and coupling; fit the reservoir, filter, relief, gauge, cooler, couplers and hoses

8327081d16fca735794a783a1254c15ff3e6d0e5.label: Power Cube: VII / 7s
8327081d16fca735794a783a1254c15ff3e6d0e5.note: Power Cube VII / 7s (v15.6, 2014–15): an 810 cc 28 hp air-cooled V-twin on a 16 cm³ gear pump, 15.2 gpm up to 3,000 psi, a 27" cube, ~181 kg; running on its sliders

assemblies.label: Frame
assemblies.note: A 27" cube: two 4×4 tube skids carry everything and take the forks; 2×2 angle posts and rails close it; the quick-attach plates on its back couple it to a machine.

assemblies.label: Engine
assemblies.note: An 810 cc air-cooled 90° V-twin, 28 hp at 3,600 rpm, electric start: its crank turns the pump through the coupling behind it.

assemblies.label: Hydraulics
assemblies.note: The gear pump on the engine’s shaft, the 7-gallon reservoir over it, the relief valve and gauge, the six-tube cooler, the return filter and the two quick couplers on the back.

assemblies.label: Fuel and controls
assemblies.note: The 7-gallon fuel tank on top, the 12 V battery, and the panel on the front corner with the key, choke and throttle.

parts.label: Base skids (4×4 tube)
parts.what: Two 4×4 steel tubes front to back under the cube: the strong frame of 7s that the engine, pump and tanks bolt to, and that takes a forklift’s forks, the lifting pins or another cube stacked on it.

parts.label: Cross tubes (2×2)
parts.what: Two 2×2 tubes welded between the skids at front and back, squaring the base.

parts.label: Corner posts (2×2 angle)
parts.what: Four corner posts of 1/4" × 2" × 2" angle make the cage: they guard the engine, carry the rails and give hand-holds to lift it by.

parts.label: Top rails (2×2 angle)
parts.what: Four rails round the top of the cage: OSE’s frame cuts its members 29", 27" and 24" long. The lifting eyes and the fuel tank’s rails hang on them.

parts.label: Fuel tank rails
parts.what: Two angles across the cage under the top, the fuel tank resting on them, clear of the engine’s air cleaner.

parts.label: Engine mount plate
parts.what: A 1/2" plate across the skids: the engine’s base bolts to it, and the pump’s bracket behind, so their shafts stay on one line.
specs: 8" × 15½" (203 × 394 mm), here one piece with the pump’s [inferred]

parts.label: Quick-attach plates and receiver
parts.what: How the cube is coupled to a machine: plates across its back with a 4×8 receiver tube between them, so it slides onto the machine’s mount and is pinned, and comes off again in minutes for the next machine.

parts.label: Lifting eyes
parts.what: Two eyes welded on the top rails: at about 181 kg the cube is lifted on and off a machine by the loader, a hoist or two people with a bar.

parts.label: Crankcase
parts.what: The engine’s cast block: it carries the crankshaft in its two main bearings, the camshaft and the governor, holds the oil in its sump, and bolts to the plate by its flange.

parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.what: One forged crank for both cylinders: their two rods share one pin, the counterweights balance them, its front end carries the flywheel and its back end drives the pump.
parts.moves: Turns at engine speed (shown slowed 40 times).
parts.drive: The pistons, through the rods; it drives the pump

parts.label: Cylinder, left
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V: a cast-iron liner the piston runs in, cast into square aluminium fins that the flywheel’s fan blows air over.

parts.label: Cylinder head, left
parts.what: The overhead-valve head: its inlet and exhaust valves under the rocker cover, the combustion chamber over the piston, and the spark plug in its front.

parts.label: Spark plug and lead, left
parts.what: The plug in the head, its boot and the lead to its ignition coil at the flywheel: a spark each turn, fired by the flywheel’s magnet.

parts.label: Piston, left
parts.what: An aluminium piston with two compression rings and an oil ring, on a hardened pin: the burning charge pushes it down 405 cm³ a stroke.
parts.moves: Up and down its cylinder, twice a turn of the crank for its four strokes.
parts.drive: The burning charge; it turns the crank through its rod

parts.label: Connecting rod, left
parts.what: The forged rod from the piston’s pin to the crank’s pin, beside its twin on the same pin.
parts.moves: Swings and slides with the crank.

parts.label: Cylinder, right
parts.what: One bank of the 90° V: a cast-iron liner the piston runs in, cast into square aluminium fins that the flywheel’s fan blows air over.

parts.label: Cylinder head, right
parts.what: The overhead-valve head: its inlet and exhaust valves under the rocker cover, the combustion chamber over the piston, and the spark plug in its front.

parts.label: Spark plug and lead, right
parts.what: The plug in the head, its boot and the lead to its ignition coil at the flywheel: a spark each turn, fired by the flywheel’s magnet.

parts.label: Piston, right
parts.what: An aluminium piston with two compression rings and an oil ring, on a hardened pin: the burning charge pushes it down 405 cm³ a stroke.
parts.moves: Up and down its cylinder, twice a turn of the crank for its four strokes.
parts.drive: The burning charge; it turns the crank through its rod

parts.label: Connecting rod, right
parts.what: The forged rod from the piston’s pin to the crank’s pin, beside its twin on the same pin.
parts.moves: Swings and slides with the crank.

parts.label: Flywheel, fan and ring gear
parts.what: Cast iron at the crank’s front: its weight smooths the twin’s firing, its magnets fire the plugs and charge the battery, its vanes are the cooling fan, and its ring gear takes the starter.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft (shown slowed 40 times).

parts.label: Rotating screen
parts.what: The perforated disc on the flywheel’s face: it turns with it and flings off grass and chaff before the fan draws its air in.
parts.moves: Turns with the flywheel.

parts.label: Blower housing
parts.what: The pressed-steel shroud over the flywheel, ducting its fan’s air back over both cylinders’ fins.

parts.label: Carburettor and intake
parts.what: In the V: the carburettor mixes petrol into the air the cleaner gives it, its throttle opened by the governor, and the manifold carries the charge to both heads.
parts.moves: Its throttle plate opens and closes with the governor.

parts.label: Air cleaner
parts.what: Over the V: a pleated paper element in a plastic cover. Every litre of air the engine breathes, about 45 litres a second at full speed, is cleaned here first.

parts.label: Muffler and exhaust
parts.what: Both exhausts into one can on the cube’s left side, the right one crossing behind the cylinders; it blows out forward, away from the couplers.

parts.label: Electric starter
parts.what: The 12 V starter whose pinion meshes with the flywheel’s ring gear while the key is held to START.
parts.moves: Spins only while starting.

parts.label: Oil filter and dipstick
parts.what: The engine’s full-pressure lubrication: a spin-on filter low on its right side, and the dipstick tube to fill and check the oil.

parts.label: Ignition coils
parts.what: One coil beside the flywheel’s rim for each plug: its magnet sweeping past them makes the spark, no battery needed.

parts.label: Governor and linkage
parts.what: Flyweights inside the crankcase push a lever out as the speed rises; its rod closes the throttle, so the engine holds its set speed whatever the pump asks, drooping a little under load.
parts.moves: Opens and closes the throttle.

parts.label: Shaft coupling
parts.what: Not a bought jaw coupling: OSE cut two coupling halves and welded them into one sleeve, keyed and set-screwed onto the engine’s shaft, splined onto the pump’s.
parts.moves: Turns with the engine (shown slowed).
parts.drive: The crankshaft; it drives the pump

parts.label: Pump bracket
parts.what: An upright plate on the engine plate holding the pump’s SAE-A flange square to the engine, so the two shafts stay on one line.
specs: SAE A: Ø 82.55 mm pilot, 2 bolts on 106.4 mm

parts.label: Hydraulic gear pump
parts.what: A fixed-displacement external gear pump: two gears mesh and carry oil round the outside of their teeth from the suction port to the pressure port, about a cubic inch every turn. This flow is everything the machine it is coupled to can do.
parts.moves: Its gears turn with the engine.
specs: 15.2 gpm (57.5 L/min) at 3,600 rpm, less its slip

parts.label: Pump gears
parts.what: The drive gear on the pump’s shaft and the idler it turns: oil trapped between their teeth and the housing is carried round the outside from suction to pressure, and the meshing teeth push it out.
parts.moves: Turn against each other at engine speed.
specs: 2π m² z b ≈ 16 cm³ a turn

parts.label: Hydraulic reservoir
parts.what: The oil tank over the pump, removable for cleaning: the pump draws through a strainer at its bottom, the returns come in at its top through the filter, and a baffle between them makes the oil settle and let go of its air before it is drawn again.

parts.label: Hydraulic oil
parts.what: About 21 L of ISO VG 46 anti-wear oil at its working level: it carries the power out to the machine and back, lubricates the pump and takes away the heat of every loss.

parts.label: Baffle and suction strainer
parts.what: A plate across the tank between the return and the suction, and a brass mesh strainer on the suction outlet at its bottom: the pump never draws air or grit.

parts.label: Suction hose
parts.what: The wide soft line from the tank’s strainer down to the pump’s inlet: wide, so the pump never starves and cavitates.

parts.label: Relief valve
parts.what: Added in October 2014: a spring-loaded poppet that opens back to the tank when the pressure reaches its setting, so nothing bursts when a cylinder bottoms out or a wheel stalls. All the power it dumps becomes heat in the oil.
parts.moves: Its poppet lifts only at its setting.

parts.label: Pressure hoses
parts.what: Two-wire braided hoses from the pump to the relief valve and on to the pressure coupler, every power stroke of the machine’s cylinders coming through them.

parts.label: Pressure gauge
parts.what: A liquid-filled gauge on the pressure line, added in April 2015: the operator sees at a glance how hard the cube is working.
parts.moves: Its needle swings with the pressure.

parts.label: Quick couplers
parts.what: The cube’s whole connection to a machine: the pressure coupler (red cap) and the return coupler (blue) on its back. Push the machine’s hoses on and the cube drives it; pull them off and it is free for the next one.

parts.label: Return hoses
parts.what: From the return coupler through the cooler and the filter back into the tank: everything the machine sends back.

parts.label: Oil cooler (six tubes)
parts.what: The 7s cooler on the cube’s right side: the returning oil runs through six finned tubes before the filter, giving the heat of every loss to the air its fan pulls through.

parts.label: Cooler fan
parts.what: The 12 V fan pulling air through the cooler’s fins into the cube.
parts.moves: Turns while the engine runs.

parts.label: Return filter
parts.what: A spin-on filter on the tank’s top where the return enters it: everything that comes back from the machine passes through it.

parts.label: Filler and breather cap
parts.what: Where the tank is filled, and how it breathes as the machine’s cylinders draw oil out and give it back.

parts.label: Sight gauge
parts.what: A window on the tank’s back above the strainer: the oil’s level and colour at a glance.

parts.label: Fuel tank
parts.what: The removable petrol tank on top of the cube, over the engine: lift it off to fill it away from the machine. Moulded of natural polyethylene, so the petrol’s level shows through its wall.

parts.label: Petrol
parts.what: The fuel at 70 % of the tank: what the engine burns, about 0.37 kg for every kWh it makes at full load.

parts.label: Fuel line and shut-off
parts.what: From the tank’s outlet down the front through a shut-off valve and an inline filter to the carburettor.

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.what: The cube’s own 12 V battery in the front corner: it cranks the starter, runs the cooler fan and the machine’s valves; the flywheel alternator charges it.

parts.label: Battery cables
parts.what: The red cable from the battery across the front to the starter’s solenoid, the black to the frame.

parts.label: Control panel
parts.what: On the front corner post: the key switch (off, run, start), the choke knob, the throttle lever that sets the governor’s speed, and an hour meter. The cube is started here and left running; the machine’s valves do the rest.
parts.moves: Key, choke and throttle are worked by hand.

steps: Cut, drill and bolt the frame: skids, posts, rails, the engine plate and the quick-attach plates
Bolt in the engine and fit its flywheel, shroud, air cleaner and muffler
Mount the coupling and the pump; fit the reservoir, hoses, relief, gauge, cooler, filter and couplers
Fit the fuel tank, the battery and the control panel

f32cc50551431c9cca7fa947e5cf768388ff897e.label: Truck: Truck
f32cc50551431c9cca7fa947e5cf768388ff897e.note: as at v1: a cab and a box trailer as plain blocks on eight wheels, in its two colours

f205c7cd0cee6caf51ddc126880040b5daee074f.label: Truck: Truck
f205c7cd0cee6caf51ddc126880040b5daee074f.note: a red cab and a white box trailer, as listed; a world gives each its colours (cab, box); 14.4 t empty, 25.6 t payload

assemblies.label: Frame and suspension
assemblies.note: The ladder frame of two C rails; the forged front axle on its leaf springs and the steering; the drive axle on its four air bellows.

assemblies.label: Wheels and brakes
assemblies.note: Six 315/70 R22.5 tyres on ten-stud steel wheels, twins on the drive axle; a disc brake worked by air at every wheel.

assemblies.label: Engine
assemblies.note: The 12.8 L six under the cab, 338 kW and 2,300 N·m, its turbocharger and its common rail.

assemblies.label: Gearbox and drive
assemblies.note: The clutch, the 12-speed automated gearbox, the propshaft and the drive axle’s gears.

assemblies.label: Cooling, fuel, air and exhaust
assemblies.note: The radiator and the charge air cooler in front of the engine, the fuel and AdBlue tanks, the batteries, the air tanks and filter, the exhaust’s aftertreatment.

assemblies.label: Cab
assemblies.note: The steel cab over the engine on two hinges and two rear mounts: its sides, face, roof and deflector, the glass, the lights, the mirrors, the bumper and the steps.

assemblies.label: Cab doors
assemblies.note: Two doors, each on two hinges at its front edge.

assemblies.label: Inside the cab
assemblies.note: The dashboard and its gauges, the steering wheel, the pedals, two seats on air, the bunk behind them.

assemblies.label: Fifth wheel and lines
assemblies.note: The fifth wheel on its mounting plate, the trailer’s kingpin locked in it, the air and electric lines between the two.

assemblies.label: Trailer chassis
assemblies.note: The trailer’s kingpin plate, its two main rails and cross members, its floor, its landing legs and its guards.

assemblies.label: Trailer axles
assemblies.note: Three axles on air bellows and trailing arms, six 385/65 R22.5 tyres, a disc brake at each.

assemblies.label: Trailer box
assemblies.note: The box on the floor: its sandwich walls and roof, its front wall, its rear frame and two doors.

parts.label: Ladder frame
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: Two pressed-steel C rails the length of the tractor, 850 mm apart outside, their webs out and their flanges in, joined by cross members riveted to them: a plate at the front for the bumper, top-hat sections over the propshaft, a deep one at the back. The springs’ hangers, the engine’s brackets, the outriggers for the steps and the tanks are riveted to the webs.

parts.label: Front axle and steering linkage
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: A forged steel I-beam across under the engine, dropped in its middle to clear the sump: a kingpin through each end carries a knuckle with its spindle, and the knuckles are tied by the tie rod behind the axle so they steer together; the drag link pulls the left one’s steering arm from the steering box.
parts.moves: Rides up and down with the road on its springs; its knuckles steer (held straight here).
parts.drive: The steering box, through the drag link

parts.label: Front springs and dampers
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: A parabolic spring each side: two tapered steel leaves clamped to the axle’s pad by four U-bolts, hung from the frame at their front eyes and swinging on shackles at their back ones as they flatten; a telescopic damper beside each.
parts.moves: They flatten as the load on the steer axle grows.

parts.label: Steering box
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: A recirculating-ball steering box with its own hydraulic power assist, bolted outside the left rail: the shaft from the steering wheel turns its worm, and its drop arm swings the drag link forward and back.
specs: Hydraulic, from a pump on the gear train [inferred]

parts.label: Drive axle
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: A pressed-steel banjo housing across the frame: in its bowl the crown wheel and the differential, the pinion in the carrier in front of it driven by the propshaft; the half-shafts through its tubes turn the hubs of the twin wheels. Single reduction, 2.53 : 1.
parts.moves: Its gears and shafts turn with the wheels.

parts.label: Crown wheel and differential
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: Inside the bowl: the pinion turns the crown wheel 2.53 times slower; the crown wheel carries the differential’s case, whose bevel gears share its push between the two half-shafts and let them turn at different speeds round a bend.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheels.

parts.label: Drive axle’s air suspension
parts.what: A trailing arm each side from a hanger on the frame, the axle clamped on it; two rolling-lobe air bellows on each arm, ahead of and behind the axle, carry the load; a levelling valve fills or empties them to hold the frame at its height whatever the load, so their pressure follows the load; a damper each side and a V-rod over the axle hold it straight.
parts.moves: The bellows’ pressure rises and falls with the load; the height stays.
parts.drive: The compressor’s air, through the levelling valve

parts.label: Wheel, front left
parts.what: A 315/70 R22.5 tubeless tyre on a 9.00 × 22.5" steel wheel, held by ten M22 nuts on studs pressed into the hub; the hub turns on two taper bearings on the spindle, and the brake disc is bolted to its back.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).
parts.drive: The road; its brake stops it

parts.label: Disc brake, front left
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: A sliding calliper over the disc’s back edge, worked by air: the chamber’s pushrod turns a lever in the calliper that presses the pads on the disc from both sides.

parts.label: Twin wheels, rear left
parts.what: Two 315/70 R22.5 tubeless tyres on 9.00 × 22.5" steel wheels, their discs back to back on the hub, held by ten M22 nuts on studs pressed into the hub; the hub turns on two taper bearings on the axle’s end, the half-shaft bolted to its cap, and the brake disc is bolted to its back.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).
