parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Cylinder block
parts.what: The cast-iron block: six bores in its deck where the wet liners stand in their coolant, the crankcase under them with seven bulkheads for the crankshaft’s main bearings, and the camshaft’s gallery along its left with the tappets’ bores up into the deck. Every other part of the engine bolts to it.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Cylinder liners
parts.what: Six wet liners of centrifugally cast iron, each a sleeve the piston runs in, its outside washed by the coolant; worn out, a liner is pulled and a new one pressed in, and the block lives on.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Bedplate and main bearing caps
parts.what: A ladder of cast iron bolted under the crankcase: seven caps that close the main bearings round the crankshaft, tied in one frame so the block does not flex at its skirts.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Crankshaft and damper
parts.what: The forged steel crankshaft on seven main journals: six throws at 120°, cylinders 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4 in pairs, turn the pistons’ push into torque, and its twelve counterweights balance them; a six in line is in balance by itself. The viscous damper on its nose calms its twisting.
parts.moves: Turns at the engine’s speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Pistons
parts.what: Six forged steel pistons, a re-entrant bowl in each crown where the injector sprays its fuel into the swirling air and it burns, three rings sealing each in its liner. The fire is drawn in a bowl as its cylinder fires, from the start of injection until the fuel has burnt.
parts.moves: Up and down their liners (shown 40 times slower); the fire in each bowl at its firing, in the order 1-5-3-6-2-4.
parts.drive: The burning charge; they drive the rods

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Connecting rods
parts.what: Forged steel I-section rods, their big ends cracked apart along a line and bolted back on their own broken faces round the crank pins, so each cap goes back exactly where it was.
parts.moves: Swing and slide with the pistons.
parts.drive: The pistons; they drive the crankshaft

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Cylinder heads
parts.what: One cast-iron head for each cylinder, held down on its gasket by four long bolts: its ports, four valves’ seats and guides round the injector’s well in its middle, and the pushrods’ passages; a head comes off alone to work on one cylinder.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Camshaft
parts.what: One camshaft low in the block, on seven bearings, turned by the gear train at half the crank’s speed: twelve lobes, an intake and an exhaust for each cylinder, each lifting its tappet at its moment of the cycle.
parts.moves: Turns at half the crank’s speed (shown slowed).
specs: opens 45° before bottom centre, closes 10° after top
opens 10° before top centre, closes 30° after bottom

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Tappets and pushrods
parts.what: A roller tappet riding on each cam lobe, sliding up its bore in the block, and a steel pushrod from it up through the head to its rocker: twelve, one for each pair of valves.
parts.moves: Rise and fall on their lobes, at the cam’s timing.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Rockers and rocker shaft
parts.what: Twelve forged rockers on one hollow shaft over the heads, oiled through it: each one’s short arm is lifted by its pushrod, its long arm presses down on a bridge, opening two valves at once by 1.17 times the cam’s lift.
parts.moves: Rock on their shaft as their pushrods rise.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Valves, springs and bridges
parts.what: Twenty-four poppet valves, two intake and two exhaust round each injector, each pair pushed open together through a bridge and shut again by its spring; the exhaust valves of heat-resistant steel.
parts.moves: Open and shut at their cam’s timing: the exhaust pair before the piston’s bottom, the intake pair before its top.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Injectors
parts.what: Six common-rail injectors stood upright in the middle of each cylinder’s four valves, their nozzles just into the bowl: the control unit opens each with a solenoid for a few thousandths of a second, and the rail’s pressure sprays its fuel through eight holes as a fine mist into the hot, squeezed air, where it lights by itself.
parts.moves: Fire in turn, at their cylinders’ top centres.
parts.drive: The control unit’s signal and the rail’s pressure

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Rocker cover
parts.what: One long moulded cover over the six heads, the rockers and the injectors, sealed on its gasket; the oil filler and the crankcase breather in it.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Gear train
parts.what: Hardened spur gears in constant mesh at the flywheel end, where the crankshaft twists least: the crank’s gear turns an idler, the idler the camshaft’s gear of twice its teeth (half the speed), and the camshaft’s gear the high-pressure pump’s and the air compressor’s.
parts.moves: Turn together with the crank (shown slowed).

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Timing gear housing
parts.what: The cast housing across the block’s back face round the gear train, its cover behind; the flywheel housing bolts to it, the pump and the compressor stand on its front face.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: High-pressure fuel pump
parts.what: A two-piston pump on the gear housing, turned by the camshaft’s gear at the crank’s speed: it squeezes the diesel the feed pump brings it to the rail’s pressure, metered by its inlet valve so it gives only what the rail needs.
parts.moves: Its shaft turns with its gear.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Common rail and fuel lines
parts.what: A forged steel tube along the engine’s left, holding the fuel at the injection pressure for all six injectors at once, its sensor at the front end and its relief valve at the back; a steel line from the pump, and six quills from the rail through the heads’ sides to the injectors.
specs: 500 to 2,400 bar, as the control unit’s map asks [inferred]

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Intake manifold
parts.what: The cast-aluminium manifold along the heads’ left side: the cooled, pressed air from the charge air cooler comes in at its front and it shares it among the six heads’ intake ports.
specs: In its inlet, for cold starts [inferred]

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Exhaust manifold
parts.what: Two cast halves, their runners on slip joints so they can grow with the heat: the front three cylinders’ gas and the back three’s kept apart into the turbine’s two inlets, so each cylinder’s pulse drives the wheel without spoiling the next. A stainless shield over it.
specs: Ductile iron with silicon and molybdenum [inferred]

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Turbocharger
parts.what: On one shaft in its oiled bearing housing: a turbine wheel of nickel alloy in the twin-entry volute, spun by the exhaust gas, and an aluminium compressor wheel in its own volute, which pulls the air in at the front and throws it out pressed. Above its boost the wastegate lets part of the gas round the turbine.
parts.moves: Its wheels spin at the speed the air model gives (shown 2,000 times slower).

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Front cover, water pump and thermostat
parts.what: The cast cover over the block’s front end round the crank’s seal and the oil pump; the water pump in it drives the coolant through the block, the liners’ jackets and the heads, and the thermostat housing on top sends it to the radiator once it is warm.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Belt drive
parts.what: One poly-V belt from the crank’s pulley round the fan’s hub, the alternator’s and the water pump’s pulleys, held tight by a spring tensioner.
parts.moves: The belt and its pulleys turn with the engine.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Alternator
parts.what: Turned by the belt at about three times the crank’s speed, it charges the 24 V batteries and runs everything electric on the truck.
parts.moves: Its rotor turns with its pulley.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Fan and viscous coupling
parts.what: Nine moulded blades, 750 mm across, on the fan hub through a viscous coupling: the silicone fluid in it locks the fan to the hub when the air through the radiator is hot and lets it slip when it is not.
parts.moves: Turns with its hub.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Sump
parts.what: The oil pan under the bedplate, deep at its back end where the oil pump’s pickup draws, shallow over the front axle; its drain plug at the bottom.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Oil cooler and filters
parts.what: A stack of plates in the coolant on the block’s right side that takes the oil’s heat into the water, and two full-flow filters hanging under its housing; the oil pump pushes all the oil through them before the bearings.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Air compressor
parts.what: A piston compressor on the gear housing, turned by the camshaft’s gear: it fills the truck’s air tanks for the brakes, the suspension, the gearbox’s shift unit and the clutch, its head cooled by the engine’s water.
parts.moves: Its crank turns with its gear.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Starter motor
parts.what: A 24 V motor on the flywheel housing: its solenoid throws its pinion into the flywheel’s ring gear and it spins the engine to start it.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Engine control unit
parts.what: The engine’s computer on rubber mounts on the block’s left: from the pedal, the boost, the temperatures and the crank’s and cam’s positions it sets the rail’s pressure and when and how long each injector opens; its harness runs to all six under the cover.
specs: Crank, cam, boost, rail, air and coolant temperatures [inferred]

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Engine mounts
parts.what: Four rubber blocks on the frame’s brackets, two at the front of the block, two at the flywheel housing: they carry 1,500 kg of engine and gearbox, take its torque and keep its shake out of the frame.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Flywheel
parts.what: A heavy steel disc on the crank’s back flange: it carries the engine through the strokes between firings and is the clutch’s friction face; the starter turns its ring gear.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Clutch
parts.what: One 430 mm friction disc pressed on the flywheel by its cover’s diaphragm spring; an air cylinder on the clutch housing pulls it apart to pull away and to change gear, so the truck has no clutch pedal.
parts.moves: Turns with the flywheel; slips while it pulls away.
parts.drive: Its air actuator, from the gearbox’s control unit

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Flywheel housing
parts.what: The cast-iron housing round the flywheel, bolted to the gear housing; the starter on it, the gearbox’s clutch housing bolted behind.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Clutch housing
parts.what: The gearbox’s cast bell bolted to the flywheel housing round the clutch, its air actuator on its side.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Gearbox, 12 speeds
parts.what: An automated 12-speed gearbox: a splitter at its front halves every step, a three-speed main box multiplies them, and a planetary range at its back multiplies them again, low or high; its control unit picks the gear and its air cylinders shift it, no lever and no pedal.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Shafts and gears
parts.what: Inside the case: the input shaft and the splitter’s two gears, the countershaft and its cluster below, the main shaft with the gears that ride free on it until a collar locks one, all in constant mesh.
parts.moves: The shafts and gears turn (shown slowed).

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Planetary range
parts.what: A sun gear on the main shaft, four planets on their carrier round it and a ring gear round them: in the low range the ring is held, and the carrier turns 4.58 times slower than the sun; in the high range the ring is locked to the carrier and all of it turns as one.
parts.moves: The sun, the planets and the carrier turn; the ring is held in the low range.

parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.label: Shift unit and control
parts.what: On the gearbox’s top: the air cylinders and valves that move its forks, and its own control unit, which picks each gear from the speed, the load and the slope and shifts it in a fraction of a second.

parts.label: Propshaft
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: A thin-walled steel tube from the gearbox to the axle’s pinion, a universal joint at each end to follow the axle as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Turns at the gearbox’s output speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.label: Radiator, charge air cooler and shroud
parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.what: In the nose under the cab’s floor, behind the grille: in front the charge air cooler, where the compressed air from the turbocharger gives its heat to the road’s air; behind it the radiator, where the engine’s coolant does; the shroud round the fan makes it pull through all of both cores.
specs: About a quarter of the fuel’s heat at full load

parts.label: Charge air pipes
parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.what: Two aluminium pipes with silicone joints: the hot, compressed air from the turbocharger round the engine’s right side to the charge air cooler, and the cooled air back round its left to the intake manifold.
specs: Up to 2.2 bar over the air’s, ~200 °C before the cooler

parts.label: Air filter and intake
parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.what: The engine breathes from an intake high on the cab’s back corner, down through a paper element in this canister behind the cab, and through a duct forward into the turbocharger’s compressor.

parts.label: Fuel tank
parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.what: A polished aluminium tank outside the left rail, hung on two brackets and two steel straps; its cap on its top outside, its sender and its pickup inside, the lines to the engine’s filters along the rail.

parts.label: Batteries
parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.what: Two 12 V batteries in series for the truck’s 24 V, in a box with a lid outside the left rail behind the tank: they start the engine and carry the cab’s load when it is off; the alternator charges them.

parts.label: AdBlue tank
parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.what: A plastic tank of urea in water outside the right rail; a pump doses it into the exhaust ahead of the SCR catalyst, where it turns the engine’s nitrogen oxides into nitrogen and water.

parts.label: Exhaust and aftertreatment
parts.source: The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)
parts.what: From the turbine down past the frame into one stainless box outside the right rail: an oxidation catalyst, the particulate filter, the AdBlue’s doser and mixer, the SCR catalyst; the tail pipe out of its bottom.
specs: DOC, DPF, SCR, ammonia slip catalyst

parts.label: Air tanks
parts.what: Two steel reservoirs across between the rails, filled by the engine’s compressor through the air dryer: they hold the air for the brakes, the bellows, the gearbox’s shift unit and the trailer’s line.

parts.label: Cab hinges, mounts and tilt ram
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: The cab rests on two hinges at the front of the frame and two sprung mounts at its back, locked down there by hooks. To reach the engine the locks open and a hand pump drives the hydraulic ram, which tilts the whole cab forward 60° on its hinges.
parts.moves: The ram stretches as the cab tilts.
specs: Coil springs and dampers at the back [inferred]

parts.label: Bumper and headlights
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: A steel bumper with its plastic skin across the front of the frame, the front underrun guard inside it; the headlights in its top corners with the indicators outside them, the fog lights below, the air dam under it.

parts.label: Steps
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: A step box each side behind the front wheel, on the frame’s outriggers: two aluminium treads at 450 and 850 mm, the third in the door’s sill at 1.25 m, the cab’s floor at 1.75 m.

parts.label: Cab sides
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The cab’s two pressed-steel sides, the door openings in them, the front wheels’ arches cut under them; the plastic wheel houses inside, round the tops of the front tyres, turning with the cab when it tilts.

parts.label: Face, roof and back
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The cab’s face with the grille’s opening low in it, the windscreen’s frame, the header over it, the high roof and the back wall of the sleeper; every edge rounded onto the sides. Under the face the apron hangs low in front of the wheels, the radiator behind it.
specs: 2.0 m standing over the flat floor

parts.label: Grille
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: Nine bars across the opening low in the cab’s face: the road’s air through them into the charge air cooler and the radiator.

parts.label: Windscreen and sun visor
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The laminated windscreen, nearly upright over the dashboard, and the sun visor over its top.

parts.label: Roof deflector
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: A glass-fibre wedge on the roof that lifts the air from the cab’s top to the trailer’s, so it does not strike the trailer’s front wall: it takes about a tenth off the drag.

parts.label: Floor and sills
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The cab’s flat steel floor over the engine, 1.75 m off the road, a rubber mat on it; each door’s sill a step lower at 1.25 m, the third of the steps; the front wall under the dashboard; the headlining under the roof and the trim on the back wall.

parts.label: Mirrors
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: On each side a main mirror and a wide-angle one under it on arms from the cab’s front corner, so the driver sees down the whole trailer and the lane beside it.

parts.label: Wipers
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: Two long wipers parked at the windscreen’s foot, driven by one motor behind the face.

parts.label: Door, left (the driver’s)
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: A hinged steel door the height of the cab’s side from its sill to its roof line, its window wound down into it by a motor, its card, armrest and handles; a grab handle down its back edge to climb the steps by.
parts.moves: Opens to 77° on its hinges.

parts.label: Door, right
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: A hinged steel door the height of the cab’s side from its sill to its roof line, its window wound down into it by a motor, its card, armrest and handles; a grab handle down its back edge to climb the steps by.
parts.moves: Opens to 77° on its hinges.

parts.label: Seats
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The driver’s seat and the passenger’s, each on its own air spring and damper so the road’s shake stops under the driver; belts built into them.

parts.label: Bunk
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The bed across the back of the cab over its lockers, where the driver sleeps through the rest the law asks for between days.

parts.label: Dashboard and gauges
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The dashboard wrapping round the driver under the windscreen: the speedometer and the rev counter before him with a screen between them, the gearbox’s selector and the switches within his reach, the passenger’s side and the shelf over the engine.
parts.moves: Its needles show the speed and the engine’s revs.
specs: Speed to 125 km/h, revs to 3,000 rpm

parts.label: Steering wheel and pedals
parts.source: Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
parts.what: The wheel laid back at a bus’s angle on its column, which a shaft carries down through the floor to the steering box; the brake and the accelerator under it (the gearbox needs no clutch pedal).
parts.moves: Turned by the driver (held straight here).

parts.label: Fifth wheel
parts.what: A greased steel plate on two pedestals that let it rock, bolted to the frame on its mounting plate: the trailer’s kingpin slides up its throat as the tractor backs under, and its jaws close round the pin; the trailer’s front rests on the plate and is pulled by the pin. A handle on its left opens the jaws.
parts.moves: Rocks on its pedestals with the road.
specs: 650 mm ahead of the drive axle

parts.label: Trailer lines and catwalk
parts.what: The catwalk behind the cab, and three coiled lines from their hanger to the trailer’s front wall: the red one supplies the trailer’s air tanks (cut it and the trailer brakes itself), the yellow one carries the brake pedal’s signal, the black one the lights and the brakes’ electronics.

parts.label: Mudguards
parts.source: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
parts.what: Plastic guards over the twin wheels on stays from the frame, and the flaps behind them that keep the spray off the road behind.

parts.label: Trailer chassis
parts.what: Two welded steel I-beams the trailer’s length, shallow over the tractor’s gooseneck and deep behind it, cross members every half metre out to the floor’s edges; at the front the kingpin plate that rests on the fifth wheel; the axles’ hangers under the beams.

parts.label: Kingpin
parts.what: A 2-inch forged steel pin under the trailer’s plate, 1.6 m behind its front: the fifth wheel’s jaws close round its neck, and through it the tractor pulls and the trailer turns.

parts.label: Floor
parts.source: Weights and dimensions of road vehicles (EU Directive 96/53/EC)
parts.what: A floor of 28 mm hardwood boards on the cross members, a fork-lift truck’s wheels’ load on any of them; lashing points along its edges.

parts.label: Landing legs
parts.what: Two telescopic legs under the trailer’s front, joined by a shaft: the crank on the right winds them down through their two-speed gearbox to stand the trailer when the tractor leaves it, and up again to drive.
parts.moves: Wound up to drive, down to park.

parts.label: Guards and lights
parts.source: Weights and dimensions of road vehicles (EU Directive 96/53/EC)
parts.what: The side guards between the landing legs and the axles that keep a cyclist from falling under the wheels; the rear underrun guard that keeps a car from running under the trailer; the tail, brake and indicator lights on it, the amber markers along the sides, and the three heads on its front wall that the tractor’s lines plug into.

parts.label: Axles and air suspension
parts.what: Three square steel axle beams, 1.31 m apart, each on two trailing arms from hangers under the main rails; an air bellows behind each axle on each arm carries the load, a levelling valve holding the trailer’s height; a damper beside each bellows; the guards over the wheels.
parts.moves: The bellows’ pressure follows the load; the height stays.
parts.drive: The road; the air from the tractor
specs: 9 t an axle, 24 t the three [inferred]

parts.label: Box walls and roof
parts.source: Weights and dimensions of road vehicles (EU Directive 96/53/EC)
parts.what: Sandwich panels of foam between two glass-fibre skins, 30 mm thick: the two sides, the front wall and the roof, bonded and riveted to aluminium rails along their edges and corners, standing on the floor’s outer rails; light, stiff and smooth to the air.

parts.label: Rear frame
parts.source: Weights and dimensions of road vehicles (EU Directive 96/53/EC)
parts.what: A galvanised steel portal at the box’s back: two corner posts carrying the doors’ hinges, the header over the opening and the sill under it, which a fork-lift truck drives over.

parts.label: Rear door, left
parts.source: Weights and dimensions of road vehicles (EU Directive 96/53/EC)
parts.what: A sandwich door on four hinges at its corner post, held shut by two locking bars whose cams turn into keepers in the header and the sill; unlocked, it swings out through 260° to lie flat against the box’s side, where a hook holds it.
parts.moves: Swings 260° on its hinges.

parts.label: Rear door, right
parts.source: Weights and dimensions of road vehicles (EU Directive 96/53/EC)
parts.what: A sandwich door on four hinges at its corner post, held shut by two locking bars whose cams turn into keepers in the header and the sill; unlocked, it swings out through 260° to lie flat against the box’s side, where a hook holds it.
parts.moves: Swings 260° on its hinges.

steps: Rivet the frame; hang the front axle on its springs and the drive axle on its air
Bolt on the wheels and brakes
Drop in the engine on its mounts
Bolt on the gearbox and the propshaft
Fit the radiator, the tanks, the batteries, the air filter and the exhaust
Lower the cab onto its hinges and mounts; fit its glass, lights, mirrors, bumper and steps
Hang the cab’s doors
Fit the dashboard, the seats and the bunk
Bolt on the fifth wheel and couple the lines
Build the trailer’s chassis and floor
Hang the trailer’s axles and wheels
Build the box on the floor and hang its doors

sources.label: Road load, grip and axle loads (Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles)
Drag of tractor-trailers (Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles)
Weights and dimensions of road vehicles (EU Directive 96/53/EC)
The engine and its turbocharger (Heywood; Watson & Janota)

de6ebda3ab0abfaaecc2b9f2e383e5ab03685c62.label: Travel van: Travel van
de6ebda3ab0abfaaecc2b9f2e383e5ab03685c62.note: 5.3 × 1.9 m, 2.13 m to its roof and 2.84 m to its bags; two-tone, faded and rusting; a sliding door and two front doors; eleven seats; 1,950 kg with its roof load

assemblies.label: Chassis and suspension
assemblies.note: The ladder frame the body sits on; double wishbones and coil springs in front with the rack-and-pinion, a live axle on leaf springs behind.

assemblies.label: Wheels and brakes
assemblies.note: Four 185/80 R14 C tyres on steel wheels; vented discs and callipers in front, drums behind.

assemblies.label: Engine
assemblies.note: A 2.4 L four-cylinder diesel under the cover between the front seats, 55 kW and 152 N·m.

assemblies.label: Gearbox and drive
assemblies.note: The clutch, the 5-speed gearbox, the two-piece propshaft and the rear axle’s crown wheel and pinion.

assemblies.label: Cooling, fuel and power
assemblies.note: The radiator and its fan in the nose, the battery and the air filter beside it, the fuel tank under the floor, the exhaust.

assemblies.label: Body
assemblies.note: The steel body in two tones on the frame: its sides, nose, roof and back, the floor, the glass.

assemblies.label: Doors
assemblies.note: The sliding door on the left and the two front doors, each on its rails or hinges.

assemblies.label: Cab and seats
assemblies.note: The dashboard and its gauges, the steering wheel and pedals, the engine’s cover, eleven seats in three rows.

assemblies.label: Roof rack and load
assemblies.note: The rack on the roof’s gutters and what is tied on it: three bags, a sack of rice and a spare tyre.

parts.label: Ladder frame
parts.what: Two box-section steel rails the length of the van, joined by crossmembers: everything hangs from it, and the body sits on it on rubber mounts. A dropped crossmember carries the front suspension under the engine’s nose, another the gearbox’s tail.

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, front left
parts.what: A 185/80 R14 tyre on a pressed-steel 14" rim, held on the hub by 5 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road and steers with the knuckle (shown turning 10 times slower).
parts.drive: The road; steered by the knuckle

parts.label: Brake disc, front left
parts.what: A vented cast-iron disc bolted to the hub between it and the wheel: the calliper squeezes it, and its vanes pump air through it to carry the heat away.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; the calliper stops it

parts.label: Brake calliper, front left
parts.what: A floating calliper over the disc’s back edge: the brake fluid pushes its piston, which presses the inner pad on the disc and pulls the outer pad on from the other side.

parts.label: Steering knuckle, front left
parts.what: The cast upright between the two wishbones’ ball joints: it carries the hub’s bearings on its spindle, the calliper on its bracket, and turns about the line through its ball joints (the kingpin axis) when the tie rod pulls its steering arm.
parts.moves: Steers about its ball joints; rides up and down with the wheel.
parts.drive: The tie rod, from the steering

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, front right
parts.what: A 185/80 R14 tyre on a pressed-steel 14" rim, held on the hub by 5 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road and steers with the knuckle (shown turning 10 times slower).
parts.drive: The road; its brake stops it

parts.label: Brake disc, front right
parts.what: A vented cast-iron disc bolted to the hub between it and the wheel: the calliper squeezes it, and its vanes pump air through it to carry the heat away.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; the calliper stops it

parts.label: Brake calliper, front right
parts.what: A floating calliper over the disc’s back edge: the brake fluid pushes its piston, which presses the inner pad on the disc and pulls the outer pad on from the other side.

parts.label: Steering knuckle, front right
parts.what: The cast upright between the two wishbones’ ball joints: it carries the hub’s bearings on its spindle, the calliper on its bracket, and turns about the line through its ball joints (the kingpin axis) when the tie rod pulls its steering arm.
parts.moves: Steers about its ball joints; rides up and down with the wheel.
parts.drive: The tie rod, from the steering

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, rear left
parts.what: A 185/80 R14 tyre on a pressed-steel 14" rim, held on the hub by 5 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).

parts.label: Brake drum, rear left
parts.what: A finned cast-iron drum on the hub: two shoes inside it, pushed out by the wheel cylinder, rub on its inner face. Cheap, sealed from the dust and good for a handbrake.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; its shoes stop it

parts.label: Backing plate, rear left
parts.what: The pressed-steel plate that closes the drum: it carries the two shoes, their springs, the wheel cylinder and the handbrake’s lever, bolted to the axle’s end.

parts.label: Wheel and tyre, rear right
parts.what: A 185/80 R14 tyre on a pressed-steel 14" rim, held on the hub by 5 nuts: its beads sit on the rim's seats, its air carries the load, its tread grips the road.
parts.moves: Rolls with the road (shown turning 10 times slower).

parts.label: Brake drum, rear right
parts.what: A finned cast-iron drum on the hub: two shoes inside it, pushed out by the wheel cylinder, rub on its inner face. Cheap, sealed from the dust and good for a handbrake.
parts.moves: Turns with the wheel.
parts.drive: The wheel; its shoes stop it

parts.label: Backing plate, rear right
parts.what: The pressed-steel plate that closes the drum: it carries the two shoes, their springs, the wheel cylinder and the handbrake’s lever, bolted to the axle’s end.

parts.label: Upper wishbone, front left
parts.what: A pressed and welded A-arm from two rubber bushes on the frame to the knuckle’s upper ball joint: with the lower arm it holds the wheel upright as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks on its springs.

parts.label: Lower wishbone, front left
parts.what: The longer, stronger lower A-arm: it carries the coil spring’s load from the knuckle’s lower ball joint to the frame and takes the braking forces.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks.

parts.label: Coil spring and damper, front left
parts.what: A coil spring round a telescopic damper from the lower arm up to its tower on the frame: the spring carries the body, the damper’s oil forced through its valves stops it bouncing.
parts.moves: Shortens as the load or the climb presses the front down; lengthens as it lifts.
parts.drive: The road, through the lower arm

parts.label: Tie rod, front left
parts.what: From the steering rack’s end to the knuckle’s steering arm: as the rack slides, it pushes or pulls the arm and turns the wheel about its ball joints. Its threaded end sets the toe.
parts.moves: Follows the rack and the wheel.

parts.label: Upper wishbone, front right
parts.what: A pressed and welded A-arm from two rubber bushes on the frame to the knuckle’s upper ball joint: with the lower arm it holds the wheel upright as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks on its springs.

parts.label: Lower wishbone, front right
parts.what: The longer, stronger lower A-arm: it carries the coil spring’s load from the knuckle’s lower ball joint to the frame and takes the braking forces.
parts.moves: Swings about its bushes as the body rises and sinks.

parts.label: Coil spring and damper, front right
parts.what: A coil spring round a telescopic damper from the lower arm up to its tower on the frame: the spring carries the body, the damper’s oil forced through its valves stops it bouncing.
parts.moves: Shortens as the load or the climb presses the front down; lengthens as it lifts.
parts.drive: The road, through the lower arm

parts.label: Tie rod, front right
parts.what: From the steering rack’s end to the knuckle’s steering arm: as the rack slides, it pushes or pulls the arm and turns the wheel about its ball joints. Its threaded end sets the toe.
parts.moves: Follows the rack and the wheel.

parts.label: Steering rack
parts.what: A rack-and-pinion box across the front: the steering wheel’s shaft turns the pinion, the pinion slides the toothed rack sideways, the rack pushes and pulls the tie rods.
parts.moves: The rack slides as the wheel is turned (held straight here).
parts.drive: The steering wheel, through its shaft and universal joints

parts.label: Rear axle housing
parts.what: The banjo housing: a pressed-steel bowl round the differential with a tube out to each wheel, its spring seats welded on. It carries the vehicle’s rear and its load straight to the wheels.

parts.label: Crown wheel, pinion and half-shafts
parts.what: The propshaft turns the pinion, the pinion turns the crown wheel 4.3 times slower and a right angle round; the differential’s gears on the crown wheel share its torque between the half-shafts, letting the outer wheel turn faster in a bend.
parts.moves: The pinion turns with the propshaft, the crown wheel and half-shafts with the wheels (shown slowed).

parts.label: Leaf springs and U-bolts
parts.what: Two packs of 5 steel leaves, each clamped to the axle by two U-bolts, its front eye on a hanger, its back eye on a swinging shackle: they carry the load and locate the axle. They flatten as the load grows.
parts.moves: Flatten as the body sinks onto the axle, arch again as it lifts.

parts.label: Spring hangers and shackles
parts.what: Under the frame: a fixed hanger for each spring’s front eye and a swinging shackle for its back eye, so the leaves can lengthen as they flatten.

parts.label: Rear dampers
parts.what: Telescopic dampers from the axle up to the frame, leaning in: oil forced through their valves turns the body’s bounce into heat.
parts.moves: Shorten as the body sinks, lengthen as it lifts.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cylinder block, 2.4 L diesel
parts.what: The cast-iron block: four 92 mm bores bored through its deck, water round them, the crankcase under them with five bulkheads that carry the crankshaft’s main bearings. Everything else on the engine bolts to it.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cylinder head
parts.what: The aluminium head closing the bores: its ports, the valves’ seats and guides, the camshaft’s bearings and the injectors’ wells; held down on its gasket by ten long bolts.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Cam cover
parts.what: The pressed cover over the camshaft and valves, keeping their oil in; its cap is where the oil goes in.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Camshaft and valves
parts.what: One overhead camshaft, turned by the timing belt at half the crank’s speed: its lobes push the eight valves open through their buckets, their springs close them.
parts.moves: Turns at half the crank’s speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.what: The forged crankshaft on its five main bearings: its four pins, two up and two down, turn the pistons’ push into torque; the counterweights opposite them balance it.
parts.moves: Turns at the engine’s speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Pistons
parts.what: Four cast-aluminium pistons, the combustion bowl in each crown where the fuel is sprayed, three rings sealing them in their bores; each pushed down by its burning charge.
parts.moves: Up and down their bores (shown 40 times slower).
parts.drive: The burning charge; they drive the rods

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Connecting rods
parts.what: Forged steel I-section rods from each piston’s pin to its crank pin, their big ends split and bolted round the pins on shell bearings.
parts.moves: Swing and slide with the pistons.
parts.drive: The pistons; they drive the crankshaft

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Flywheel
parts.what: A heavy steel disc on the crank’s back end: it carries the engine through the strokes between firings and is the clutch’s friction face; the starter turns its ring gear.
parts.moves: Turns with the crankshaft.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Clutch
parts.what: A friction disc pressed against the flywheel by the cover’s diaphragm spring: it passes the engine’s torque to the gearbox, and slips to let the vehicle pull away.
parts.moves: Turns with the flywheel; slips while it pulls away.
parts.drive: The pedal, through its cable and release bearing

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Sump
parts.what: The pressed-steel oil pan under the crankcase, deep at one end where the pump’s pickup draws the oil; its drain plug at the bottom.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Timing belt and cover
parts.what: A toothed belt from the crank to the camshaft and the injection pump, both turning at half the crank’s speed so each valve and each squirt of fuel comes at its stroke; under its plastic cover.
parts.moves: The belt runs round its three sprockets.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Accessory belt and water pump
parts.what: A V-belt from the crank’s pulley (its damper behind) round the water pump’s and the alternator’s: the pump drives the coolant through the block, the head and the radiator.
parts.moves: The belt and pulleys turn with the engine.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Alternator
parts.what: Turned by the belt at about 2.5 times the crank’s speed, it charges the battery and runs the lights.
parts.moves: Its rotor and pulley turn with the belt.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Injection pump, lines and injectors
parts.what: The distributor pump, turned by the timing belt, meters the fuel and squeezes it to some 300 bar into each injector in turn through its own steel line, at the moment its piston comes up on compression; the glow plugs on the other side warm the chambers for a cold start.
parts.moves: Its shaft turns at half the crank’s speed.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Intake manifold
parts.what: The cast-aluminium manifold that shares the air from the filter among the four inlet ports.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Exhaust manifold
parts.what: The cast-iron manifold gathering the four cylinders’ hot gas into the downpipe.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Oil filter and dipstick
parts.what: A spin-on full-flow filter that the oil pump pushes all the oil through before the bearings; the dipstick to check its level.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Starter motor
parts.what: A 12 V motor on the bellhousing’s flange: its solenoid throws its pinion into the flywheel’s ring gear and it spins the engine to start it.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Engine and gearbox mounts
parts.what: Rubber blocks between the engine’s brackets and the frame, and under the gearbox’s tail: they carry its weight and its torque and keep its shake out of the body.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Bellhousing
parts.what: The cast-aluminium bell bolted to the block’s back face round the flywheel and clutch, carrying the gearbox and the starter.

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Gearbox, 5 speeds
parts.what: A 5-speed manual gearbox: the input shaft from the clutch drives the layshaft below it, whose gears turn the gears riding free on the output shaft; the lever slides a synchro collar to lock one of them to the shaft (top gear locks the input to the output straight).

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Shafts and gears
parts.what: Inside the case: the input shaft and its gear, the layshaft and its cluster, the output shaft with the gears that ride on it, all in constant mesh; the synchro collars between them.
parts.moves: The shafts and gears turn (shown 40 times slower).
specs: Constant, helical in the case [simplified straight here]

parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.label: Gear lever
parts.what: The lever and its rod into the gearbox’s selector: across to pick a gate, forward and back to choose a gear.
parts.moves: Moved by hand; the solver changes gear by itself.

parts.label: Propshaft (two pieces)
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: Two thin-walled steel tubes from the gearbox to the axle, joined over a rubber-mounted centre bearing under the floor, a universal joint at each end of each to follow the axle as it rises and falls.
parts.moves: Turns at the gearbox’s output speed (shown 40 times slower).

parts.label: Radiator and fan
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: In the nose behind the grille: the engine’s coolant runs down through the radiator’s finned tubes and gives its heat to the air the road and the electric fan push through it; two long hoses run back under the floor to the engine.
parts.moves: The fan turns when the coolant is hot.
parts.drive: Its 12 V motor, switched by a thermostat
specs: About a third of the fuel’s heat at full load

parts.label: 12 V battery
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: The starting battery in the nose, beside the radiator: it cranks the engine and heats the glow plugs; the alternator charges it.

parts.label: Air filter and intake
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: The engine breathes through a paper element in this box behind the grille, then down a long duct to the intake manifold.

parts.label: Fuel tank
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: A 60 L pressed-steel tank under the floor on the right, hung on two straps; its filler neck runs up to the cap on the side.

parts.label: Exhaust and silencer
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: From the manifold down and back under the floor through the silencer, over the axle and out under the back on the right, hung on rubber loops.

parts.label: Body sides
parts.what: The two pressed-steel sides, cream below the waist and blue above, their windows, door openings and wheel arches cut in; the wheel housings inside. Thirty years of sun have faded the blue, and the sills and arches are rusting through.

parts.label: Side windows
parts.what: Fixed side windows of toughened glass in rubber seals.

parts.label: Nose, roof and back
parts.what: The body’s ends and top: the short nose with the grille’s opening, the bonnet, the windscreen’s frame, the roof, and the back with its two doors (shut here); every edge rounded onto the sides.

parts.label: Windscreen and back window
parts.what: The laminated windscreen, nearly upright over the short nose, and the back window between the rear doors.

parts.label: Floor
parts.what: The ribbed steel floor on the frame, cut round the engine’s cover and the wheel housings, a rubber mat over it; the wall under the dashboard closes the cab from the nose.

parts.label: Bumpers and number plates
parts.what: Steel bumpers front and back on brackets to the frame, painted black; the plates (blank) on them.

parts.label: Lights and grille
parts.what: Two square sealed-beam headlights with their indicators under them in the nose, the grille between them that lets the air to the radiator; the tail lights, indicators and reversing lights at the back corners.

parts.label: Gutters and wipers
parts.what: The rain gutters along the roof’s edges, where the rack’s feet clamp; the two wipers on the windscreen.

parts.label: Front door, left
parts.what: A hinged steel door over the front wheel, its window wound down by a handle inside; its mirror on its front corner. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Front door, right (the driver’s)
parts.what: A hinged steel door over the front wheel, its window wound down by a handle inside; its mirror on its front corner. It swings out on two hinges at its front edge.
parts.moves: Opens to 70° on its hinges.

parts.label: Sliding door
parts.what: The wide door on the left into the seats behind: its rollers run in three rails, top, bottom and the centre rail along the side, that first pull it out of its opening and then slide it back along the van.
parts.moves: Out of its opening, then back along the side (the Doors slider).

parts.label: Engine cover
parts.source: Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)
parts.what: The padded box between the front seats over the engine (the “doghouse”): lift it off to reach the engine from inside; its lining keeps the noise and heat out of the cab.

parts.label: Front seats
parts.what: The driver’s seat and one passenger’s, each side of the engine’s cover, on pedestals over the front wheel housings.

parts.label: Middle bench
parts.what: A bench for three behind the front seats, an aisle beside it to the sliding door.

parts.label: Rear bench
parts.what: The full-width bench at the back, over the rear axle’s front; the luggage behind it.

parts.label: Dashboard and gauges
parts.what: The moulded dashboard under the windscreen: the speedometer and the rev counter in their binnacle before the driver, the radio, four vents, the glovebox.
parts.moves: Its needles show the speed and the engine’s revs.
specs: Speed to 140 km/h, revs to 5,000 rpm

parts.label: Steering wheel and column
parts.what: A large, nearly flat wheel, as on a bus, on its column down to the floor, where a shaft with two universal joints runs to the rack.
parts.moves: Turned by the driver (held straight here).

parts.label: Pedals and handbrake

steps: Weld the frame and hang the suspension, the axle and the steering on it
Bolt on the wheels and brakes
Drop in the engine on its mounts
Bolt on the gearbox; fit the propshaft and the axle’s gears
Fit the radiator, battery, fuel tank and exhaust
Lower the body onto the frame; fit the glass
Hang the doors
Fit the dashboard, the steering wheel, the seats
Bolt on the roof rack and tie the load on

Engine friction and fuel (Heywood, IC Engine Fundamentals)

3963d2f55c551a79ffb2e9046bdfa2946ed0298b.label: Bell tent
3963d2f55c551a79ffb2e9046bdfa2946ed0298b.note: The Buildings’ bell tent made a model in its 20 parts, pitched step by step: the groundsheet, the canvas spread, the pole walked up, the wall poles and pegs, the guy ropes, the door rolled back, the things brought in and the lantern lit

assemblies.label: Groundsheet
assemblies.note: What it stands on: the bathtub groundsheet and the pegs that hold it down.

assemblies.label: Canvas
assemblies.note: One piece of cotton canvas sewn from twelve panels: the bell, the wall below it, the door in both.

assemblies.label: Poles
assemblies.note: The centre pole the whole tent hangs from, and the short wall poles under its eave.

assemblies.label: Ropes and pegs
assemblies.note: What holds it to the ground and keeps the canvas tight: the guy ropes, their runners and pegs, the wall pegs.

assemblies.label: Inside
assemblies.note: What is brought in once it stands: two beds at the back, a table, the packs, the lantern.

parts.label: Groundsheet
parts.what: Heavy PVC, round, 4.2 m across, its edge turned up 15 cm into a tub so no water runs in; zipped to the foot of the wall all round.

parts.label: Groundsheet pegs
parts.what: A plastic hook peg through a rubber ring at each D-ring round the groundsheet’s edge: the rubber gives, so the sheet is held without tearing.

parts.label: Bell
parts.what: The roof: twelve panels of 285 g/m² cotton canvas sewn into a bell, rising from the eave to a leather-backed cap round the pole’s spike. It glows from inside at night.
parts.moves: Rises on the centre pole as it is walked upright

parts.label: Wall
parts.what: The same canvas hanging 75 cm from the eave to the ground, all round but for the door, pegged out at its foot; zipped to the groundsheet.
parts.moves: Hangs loose until the wall poles push the eave up and its foot is pegged

parts.label: Door flaps
parts.what: The door, 1.1 m wide and 1.8 m high, closes with two flaps zipped down its middle; by day they are rolled back to either side and tied with their ties.
parts.moves: Roll back to the sides of the door and are tied

parts.label: Centre pole
parts.what: Ash, 70 mm round and 3.15 m long in three sections joined by steel ferrules; a spike at its top through the canvas’s cap, a rubber foot.
parts.moves: Walked upright from lying, its top under the cap, its foot sliding in to the middle

parts.label: Wall poles
parts.what: Short poles standing just inside the wall under the eave, each with a spike through the eyelet at a guy rope’s loop: they hold the eave up so the wall hangs straight.
parts.moves: Stood up one by one

parts.label: Guy ropes
parts.what: Ten 8 mm polyester ropes from the wall poles’ spikes out to their pegs; tight, they pull the eave out and keep the canvas taut in the wind.
parts.moves: Run out to their pegs and tensioned

parts.label: Runners
parts.what: A wooden runner on each guy rope: slid along it, it pulls the rope tight or lets it off as the canvas shrinks in the rain and dries.
parts.moves: Slid along its rope to tension it

parts.label: Guy pegs
parts.what: Steel pegs 30 cm long, knocked in at 45° leaning away from the tent, so the rope pulls them down into the ground and not out of it.

parts.label: Wall pegs
parts.what: Steel pin pegs through the loops at the wall’s foot, all round but for the door.

parts.label: Rug
parts.what: A round jute rug 1.8 m across in front of the beds.

parts.label: Mats
parts.what: Two foam sleeping mats, 62 cm wide and 1.9 m long, at the back.

parts.label: Sleeping bags
parts.what: Two sleeping bags on the mats, one teal and one rust.

parts.label: Pillows
parts.what: Two linen pillows at the head of the beds, by the wall.

parts.label: Crate
parts.what: A wooden crate 50 × 36 cm on its side for a table, by the door.

parts.label: Mugs
parts.what: Two white enamel mugs with blue rims on the crate.

parts.label: Book
parts.what: A book left on the crate.

parts.label: Packs
parts.what: Two packs against the wall, olive and brown.

parts.label: Lantern
parts.what: A green hurricane lantern hung from a hook on the pole at 2 m, its flame behind glass: the light inside the tent, and the glow of the canvas at night.
parts.moves: Hung on its hook and lit

steps: Lay the groundsheet out where the tent will stand, its door to the front, unfold it and peg it down through the rings round its edge.
Spread the canvas over it, its door over the groundsheet’s door.
Crawl in under the canvas with the centre pole, put its spike through the cap at the top and walk it upright: the canvas rises on it.
Stand a wall pole under the eave at each guy rope’s loop, its spike through the eyelet, then peg the wall’s foot out round the groundsheet.
Run each guy rope out from its wall pole, knock its peg in at 45° 1.5 m out from the wall, loop the rope over it and pull it tight with its runner.
Roll the door flaps back to either side of the door and tie them.
Bring the things in: the rug, two mats and sleeping bags with their pillows, the crate with two mugs and a book, the packs; hang the lantern on the pole and light it.

assemblies.label: Woodpile
assemblies.note: Split logs stacked to dry, within reach of the fire.

parts.label: Stones
parts.what: Field stones the size of a loaf set round the fire, 1.2 m across: they keep the embers in and the grass out.

parts.label: Bed of ash
parts.what: The bare earth inside the ring, grey with old ash; it glows where the embers lie.
parts.moves: Glows as the fire burns down

parts.label: Logs
parts.what: Four split logs, 80 cm long, leant together over the kindling so the air draws up through them.

parts.label: Flames
parts.what: The fire itself and its light: warm, flickering, lighting the ground about 7 m round.
parts.moves: Flicker; grow when it is lit, die down when it is put out

parts.label: Chairs
parts.what: Two green folding camp chairs, the seats at 40 cm, facing the fire.
parts.moves: Unfold

parts.label: Woodpile
parts.what: Nine split logs 60 cm long, three rows of three on two bearers off the ground.

steps: Clear a round of earth and set a ring of stones round it, 1.2 m across.
Stack the woodpile beside it, split logs three rows high.
Lay four logs over the kindling in a tepee.
Unfold the two chairs facing the fire.
Light the kindling.
